title.zh: 卷七十八 列傳第六十八 夷貊上
title.raw: 卷七十八 列傳第六十八 夷貊上 Volume 78 Biographies 68: Non-Han Peoples 1

sentences.zh: 海南諸國

translations.literal: The Various Countries South of the Sea
translations.idiomatic: The Countries of the Southern Seas

sentences.zh: 海南諸國

translations.literal: The Various Countries South of the Sea
translations.idiomatic: The Countries of the Southern Seas

sentences.zh: 海南諸國，大抵在交州南及西南大海洲上，相去或四五千里，遠者二三萬里。

translations.literal: The various countries south of the sea are for the most part located south and southwest of Jiaozhou on great islands in the ocean, separated by perhaps four or five thousand li, and in distant cases twenty or thirty thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdoms of the southern seas lie for the most part south and southwest of Jiaozhou on great ocean islands, anywhere from four or five thousand li apart to as much as twenty or thirty thousand li in the farthest cases.

sentences.zh: 其西與西域諸國接。

translations.literal: To their west they border the various countries of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: To the west they adjoin the states of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 漢元鼎中，遣伏波將軍路博多開百越，置日南郡。

translations.literal: In the Yuanding era of Han, they dispatched the Pacification Army general Lu Bodede to open the Hundred Yue, and established Rinan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanding reign of the Han, the court sent the Pacification Army general Lu Bodede to subdue the Hundred Yue and established Rinan commandery.

sentences.zh: 其徼外諸國，自武帝以來皆朝貢。

translations.literal: The various countries beyond the frontier, from Emperor Wu onward all came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From the reign of Emperor Wu onward, the states beyond the frontier all sent tribute missions to court.

sentences.zh: 後漢桓帝世，大秦、天竺皆由此道遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Huan of Later Han, Daqin and Tianzhu both sent envoys by this route to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huan of the Later Han, Daqin and India both dispatched envoys along this route to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 及吳孫權時，遣宣化從事朱應、中郎康泰通焉。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan of Wu was in power, he dispatched the Pacification Commissioner Zhu Ying and the Gentleman Kang Tai to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Quan of Wu, the court sent the Pacification Commissioner Zhu Ying and the Gentleman Kang Tai to travel there.

sentences.zh: 其所經過及傳聞則有百數十國，因立記傳。

translations.literal: The countries they passed through and heard of numbered more than a hundred, and on that basis they composed a written account.
translations.idiomatic: The lands they visited and learned of by report numbered well over a hundred, and they compiled a written record of them.

sentences.zh: 晉代通中國者蓋鮮，故不載史官。

translations.literal: In the Jin era those communicating with China were few, and therefore they were not recorded by the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin, contact with China was sparse, so the historiographers did not record these states.

sentences.zh: 及宋、齊至梁，其奉正朔、修貢職，航海往往至矣。

translations.literal: From Song and Qi down to Liang, those who accepted the imperial calendar and fulfilled tribute duties often arrived by sea voyage.
translations.idiomatic: From the Song and Qi dynasties through Liang, states that acknowledged the imperial calendar and paid tribute often reached China by sea.

sentences.zh: 今采其風俗粗著者列為海南云。

translations.literal: Now I gather those whose customs are roughly notable and list them under the heading of the Southern Seas.
translations.idiomatic: Here I collect those whose customs are sufficiently distinctive and present them under the rubric of the Southern Seas.

sentences.zh: 林邑國

translations.literal: The State of Linyi
translations.idiomatic: The Kingdom of Linyi

sentences.zh: 林邑國，本漢日南郡象林縣，古越裳界也。

translations.literal: The state of Linyi was originally Xianglin county of Rinan commandery in Han, the borderland of ancient Yuechang.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi had originally been Xianglin county in Han Rinan commandery, on the frontier of ancient Yuechang.

sentences.zh: 伏波將軍馬援開南境，置此縣。

translations.literal: The Pacification Army general Ma Yuan opened the southern frontier and established this county.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Army general Ma Yuan opened the southern frontier and founded this county.

sentences.zh: 其地從廣可六百里。

translations.literal: Its territory from east to west was about six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory measured roughly six hundred li from east to west.

sentences.zh: 城去海百二十里，去日南南界四百餘里，北接九德郡。

translations.literal: The capital was one hundred twenty li from the sea, more than four hundred li from the southern border of Rinan, and adjoined Jiude commandery to the north.
translations.idiomatic: The capital stood one hundred twenty li from the sea, more than four hundred li south of the Rinan border, and bordered Jiude commandery on the north.

sentences.zh: 其南界，水步道二百餘里，有西圖夷亦稱王，馬援所植二銅柱，表漢家界處也。

translations.literal: On its southern border, two hundred-odd li by water and land route, there were the Xitu Yi who also styled themselves kings; the two bronze pillars planted by Ma Yuan marked the boundary of the Han domain.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred-odd li along the southern border by water and trail lived the Xitu Yi, who likewise called themselves kings; the pair of bronze pillars Ma Yuan had erected marked the Han frontier.

sentences.zh: 其國有金山，石皆赤色，其中生金。

translations.literal: In that state there was a Golden Mountain; its stones were all reddish, and gold was produced within them.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom had a Golden Mountain whose stones were all reddish and yielded gold within.

sentences.zh: 金夜則出飛，狀如螢火。

translations.literal: At night the gold would fly forth, in appearance like fireflies.
translations.idiomatic: At night the gold would rise and drift about like fireflies.

sentences.zh: 又出瓄瑁、貝齒、古貝、沈木香。

translations.literal: It also produced tortoise shell, cowrie shells, kapok, and agarwood.
translations.idiomatic: It also exported tortoise shell, cowries, kapok fiber, and agarwood.

sentences.zh: 古貝者，樹名也，其華成時如鵝毳，抽其緒紡之以作布，布與紵布不殊。

translations.literal: Kapok is the name of a tree; when its blossoms mature they are like goose down, and drawing out the fibers one spins them to make cloth, cloth not different from ramie cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Kapok is a tree whose blossoms, when mature, resemble goose down; the fibers are spun into cloth indistinguishable from ramie.

sentences.zh: 亦染成五色，織為斑布。

translations.literal: It is also dyed in five colors and woven into patterned cloth.
translations.idiomatic: It is also dyed in five colors and woven into variegated cloth.

sentences.zh: 沈木香者，土人斫斷，積以歲年，朽爛而心節獨在，置水中則沈，故名曰沈香，次浮者棧香。

translations.literal: As for agarwood, the natives cut and break it, pile it up over years; when rotten the heartwood alone remains; placed in water it sinks, and therefore is called sinking incense; that which floats next is called stack incense.
translations.idiomatic: For agarwood, locals cut the timber and stack it for years until the outer wood rots away and only the heart remains; placed in water it sinks, hence the name sinking incense, while the lighter grade that floats is called stack incense.

sentences.zh: 漢末大亂，功曹區連殺縣令，自立為王。

translations.literal: At the end of Han in great disorder, the Clerk of Merit Qu Lian killed the magistrate and established himself as king.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han collapsed into chaos, the Clerk of Merit Qu Lian murdered the county magistrate and declared himself king.

sentences.zh: 數世，其後王無嗣，外甥范熊代立，死，子逸嗣。

translations.literal: After several generations the later king had no heir; the nephew Fan Xiong replaced him on the throne, died, and his son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After several generations a king died without heirs, and his nephew Fan Xiong took the throne; when Fan Xiong died, his son Yi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康三年，逸死，奴文篡立。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiankang of Emperor Cheng of Jin, Yi died and the slave Wen usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin, Yi died and Wen the slave seized power.

sentences.zh: 文本日南西卷縣夷帥范幼家奴，嘗牧牛於山澗，得鱧魚二化而為鐵，因以鑄刀。

translations.literal: Wen was originally a household slave of Fan You, a Yi chieftain of Juan county west of Rinan; he once herded cattle in mountain streams, obtained two snakehead fish that transformed into iron, and on that basis cast a knife.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had been a household slave of Fan You, a tribal leader in Juan county west of Rinan; while herding cattle in the hills he caught two snakehead fish that turned to iron, which he used to forge a knife.

sentences.zh: 刀成，文向石祝曰：「若斫石破者，文當王此國。」

translations.literal: When the knife was finished, Wen prayed to a stone, saying: "If I chop the stone and it breaks, Wen shall become king of this state."
translations.idiomatic: When the blade was finished, Wen prayed to a stone: "If this stone splits when I strike it, I shall rule this kingdom."

sentences.zh: 因斫石如斷芻稿，文心異之。

translations.literal: He then chopped the stone as if cutting dried fodder, and Wen marveled in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He struck the stone and it split as easily as dry straw, and Wen took this as a wondrous sign.

sentences.zh: 範幼嘗使之商賈至林邑，因教林邑王作宮室及兵車器械，王寵任之。

translations.literal: Fan You once sent him on trading missions to Linyi, and he thereby taught the king of Linyi to build palaces and military vehicles and weapons; the king favored and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan You had once sent him to trade in Linyi, where he taught the Linyi king how to build palaces and military equipment; the king came to favor and rely on him.

sentences.zh: 後乃讒言諸子，各奔余國。

translations.literal: Later he slandered the princes, and each fled to other states.
translations.idiomatic: Later he slandered the princes until each fled to a neighboring kingdom.

sentences.zh: 及王死無嗣，文偽于鄰國迓王子，置毒於漿中殺之，遂脅國人自立。

translations.literal: When the king died without heirs, Wen pretended in a neighboring state to welcome the prince, placed poison in gruel and killed him, then coerced the people of the state to establish himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the king died childless, Wen pretended in a neighboring state to escort the heir home, poisoned his gruel and killed him, then forced the people to accept him as ruler.

sentences.zh: 時交州刺史姜莊使所親韓戢、謝幼前後監日南郡，並貪殘，諸國患之。

translations.literal: At that time the Inspector of Jiaozhou Jiang Zhuang sent his intimates Han Ji and Xie You in succession to supervise Rinan commandery; both were greedy and cruel, and the various states suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaozhou inspector Jiang Zhuang had sent his favorites Han Ji and Xie You, in turn, to oversee Rinan; both were rapacious, and the frontier states groaned under them.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和三年，台遣夏侯覽為太守，侵刻尤盛。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghe of Emperor Mu, the court dispatched Xiahou Lan as administrator, and his encroachments and extortions were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu, the court appointed Xiahou Lan administrator, and his exactions were worse still.

sentences.zh: 林邑素無田土，貪日南地肥沃，常欲略有之。

translations.literal: Linyi from of old had no arable land of its own and coveted the fertile soil of Rinan, constantly wishing to seize it in part.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi had never possessed enough arable land of its own and coveted the fertile fields of Rinan, always seeking to seize them.

sentences.zh: 至是因人之怨，襲殺覽，以其屍祭天。

translations.literal: At this point, taking advantage of popular resentment, he raided and killed Lan and used his corpse to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing on popular resentment, he attacked and killed Lan and offered his corpse in sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 留日南三年，乃還林邑。

translations.literal: He remained in Rinan three years, then returned to Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: He held Rinan for three years before returning to Linyi.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史朱藩後遣督護劉雄戍日南，文復滅之，進寇九德郡，害吏人。

translations.literal: Later the Inspector of Jiaozhou Zhu Fan dispatched the Commandant-Protector Liu Xiong to garrison Rinan; Wen again destroyed him, advanced to raid Jiude commandery, and harmed officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Jiaozhou inspector Zhu Fan sent Commandant-Protector Liu Xiong to garrison Rinan; Wen destroyed his force, pushed into Jiude commandery, and killed officials and civilians.

sentences.zh: 遣使告藩，願以日南北境橫山為界。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to inform Fan, wishing to take Mount Heng on the northern border of Rinan as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to Zhu Fan proposing Mount Heng on Rinan's northern border as the frontier.

sentences.zh: 藩不許。

translations.literal: Fan did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Fan refused.

sentences.zh: 文歸林邑，尋復屯日南。

translations.literal: Wen returned to Linyi, but soon again encamped in Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen withdrew to Linyi but soon encamped in Rinan again.

sentences.zh: 文死，子佛立，猶屯日南。

translations.literal: When Wen died, his son Fo established himself, still encamped in Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen died, his son Fo succeeded him and still held camp in Rinan.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍桓溫遣督護滕畯、九真太守灌邃討之，追至林邑，佛乃請降。

translations.literal: The Western Campaign general Huan Wen dispatched the Commandant-Protector Teng Jun and the Administrator of Jiuzhen Guan Sui to attack him; pursuing to Linyi, Fo then requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Campaign general Huan Wen sent Commandant-Protector Teng Jun and the Jiuzhen administrator Guan Sui against him; pursued to Linyi, Fo sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 安帝隆安三年，佛孫須達復寇日南、九德諸郡，無歲不至，殺傷甚多，交州遂致虛弱。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longan of Emperor An, Fo's grandson Xuda again raided Rinan, Jiude, and the various commanderies; not a year passed without his coming, and casualties were many; Jiaozhou thus became enfeebled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Longan under Emperor An, Fo's grandson Xuda raided Rinan and Jiude year after year, inflicting heavy casualties until Jiaozhou was thoroughly weakened.

sentences.zh: 須達死，子敵真立，其弟敵鎧攜母出奔。

translations.literal: When Xuda died, his son Dizhen established himself; his younger brother Dikai took their mother and fled abroad.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuda died, his son Dizhen took the throne while his younger brother Dikai fled abroad with their mother.

sentences.zh: 敵真追恨不能容其母弟，舍國而之天竺，禪位於其甥。

translations.literal: Dizhen, pursuing regret that he could not accommodate his mother and younger brother, abandoned the state and went to Tianzhu, ceding the throne to his nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Tormented that he had driven out his mother and brother, Dizhen abandoned the kingdom for India and abdicated in favor of his nephew.

sentences.zh: 國相藏驎固諫不從。

translations.literal: The Chancellor Zang Lin firmly remonstrated but was not obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor Zang Lin protested strenuously, but Dizhen would not listen.

sentences.zh: 其甥立而殺藏驎，藏驎子又攻殺之，而立敵鎧同母異父弟曰文敵。

translations.literal: The nephew upon establishing himself killed Zang Lin; Zang Lin's son in turn attacked and killed him, and established Dikai's younger brother by the same mother but different father, named Wen Di.
translations.idiomatic: The nephew took the throne and murdered Zang Lin; Zang Lin's son killed the nephew in turn and installed Dikai's younger half-brother, Wen Di.

sentences.zh: 文敵復為扶南王子當根純所殺，大臣范諸農平其亂，自立為王。

translations.literal: Wen Di was again killed by the Funan prince Danggen Chun; the great minister Fan Zhunong pacified the disorder and established himself as king.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Di was then killed by the Funan prince Danggen Chun; the senior minister Fan Zhunong quelled the turmoil and made himself king.

sentences.zh: 諸農死，子陽邁立。

translations.literal: When Zhunong died, his son Yangmai established himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhunong died, his son Yangmai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 陽邁初在孕，其母夢生兒，有人以金席藉之，其色光麗。

translations.literal: When Yangmai was first in the womb, his mother dreamed she gave birth to a child and someone spread a golden mat beneath him, its color bright and lustrous.
translations.idiomatic: While Yangmai was still in the womb, his mother dreamed of giving birth to a child laid on a golden mat of dazzling brilliance.

sentences.zh: 夷人謂金之精者為陽邁，若中國雲紫磨者，因以為名。

translations.literal: The Yi call the finest essence of gold Yangmai, like the purple-polished gold of China, and on that basis gave him the name.
translations.idiomatic: The natives call the finest gold yangmai, comparable to the finest purple-polished gold in China, and they gave him that name.

sentences.zh: 宋永初二年，遣使貢獻，以陽邁為林邑王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu of Song, he sent envoys with tribute, and Yangmai was enfeoffed as King of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu of Song he sent tribute envoys, and Yangmai was invested as King of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 陽邁死，子咄立，慕其父復曰陽邁。

translations.literal: When Yangmai died, his son Zhuo established himself; admiring his father, he again took the name Yangmai.
translations.idiomatic: When Yangmai died, his son Zhuo succeeded and, in admiration of his father, adopted the name Yangmai himself.

sentences.zh: 其國俗，居處為閣，名曰幹闌。

translations.literal: The customs of that state: dwellings are pavilions, called ganlan.
translations.idiomatic: In that kingdom people live in raised pavilions called ganlan.

sentences.zh: 門戶皆北向。

translations.literal: Doors and gates all face north.
translations.idiomatic: All doors and gates face north.

sentences.zh: 書樹葉為紙。

translations.literal: They write on tree leaves as paper.
translations.idiomatic: They write on leaves in place of paper.

sentences.zh: 男女皆以橫幅古貝繞腰以下，謂之幹漫，亦曰都漫。

translations.literal: Men and women all wrap kapok cloth in horizontal bands below the waist, called ganman, also called duman.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women alike wrap a band of kapok cloth below the waist, called ganman or duman.

sentences.zh: 穿耳貫小環。

translations.literal: They pierce the ears and thread small rings.
translations.idiomatic: They pierce their ears and wear small rings.

sentences.zh: 貴者著革屣，賤者跣行。

translations.literal: The noble wear leather sandals; the lowly go barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: The elite wear leather sandals; commoners go barefoot.

sentences.zh: 自林邑、扶南以南諸國皆然也。

translations.literal: From Linyi and Funan southward all the states are thus.
translations.idiomatic: The same customs prevail in all kingdoms from Linyi and Funan southward.

sentences.zh: 其王者著法服，加瓔珞，如佛像之飾。

translations.literal: Their kings wear ritual robes and add jeweled chains, like the adornments of a Buddha image.
translations.idiomatic: Their kings wear ceremonial robes hung with jeweled chains, much like the adornments on a Buddha image.

sentences.zh: 出則乘象，吹螺擊鼓，罩古貝傘，以古貝為幡旗。

translations.literal: When going out they ride elephants, blow conches and strike drums, cover themselves with kapok umbrellas, and use kapok for banners and flags.
translations.idiomatic: When the king goes abroad he rides an elephant to the sound of conches and drums, shaded by a kapok umbrella and preceded by kapok banners.

sentences.zh: 國不設刑法，有罪者使象蹋殺之。

translations.literal: The state establishes no penal code; those guilty are made to be trampled to death by elephants.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom has no written penal code; offenders are trampled to death by elephants.

sentences.zh: 其大姓號婆羅門，嫁娶必用八月。

translations.literal: Their great clans are called Brahman; marriage must take place in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: The great clans are called Brahman, and weddings must be held in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 女先求男，由賤男而貴女。

translations.literal: Women first seek out men; men are held cheap and women precious.
translations.idiomatic: Women take the initiative in courtship, for men are held cheap and women precious.

sentences.zh: 同姓還相婚姻。

translations.literal: Those of the same surname still marry one another.
translations.idiomatic: People of the same surname may marry one another.

sentences.zh: 使婆羅門引婿見婦，握手相付，祝曰：「吉利吉利。」

translations.literal: They have a Brahman lead the groom to see the bride; they clasp hands and entrust themselves to each other, praying: "Auspicious, auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: A Brahman leads the groom to the bride; they clasp hands and the priest blesses them: "Good fortune, good fortune."

sentences.zh: 為成禮。

translations.literal: This constitutes completion of the rites.
translations.idiomatic: With that the marriage rite is complete.

sentences.zh: 死者焚之中野，謂之火葬。

translations.literal: The dead are burned in the open wilds, called fire burial.
translations.idiomatic: The dead are cremated in the open country, a practice called fire burial.

sentences.zh: 其寡婦孤居，散發至老。

translations.literal: Their widows dwell alone, with hair unbound until old age.
translations.idiomatic: Widows live alone with their hair unbound until they grow old.

sentences.zh: 國王事尼幹道，鑄金銀人像大十圍。

translations.literal: The king served the Nigan Way and cast gold and silver human images ten arm-spans tall.
translations.idiomatic: The king followed the Nigan teaching and cast gold and silver statues ten arm-spans high.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，陽邁侵暴日南、九德諸郡，交州刺史杜弘文建牙欲討之，聞有代乃止。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia, Yangmai invaded and ravaged Rinan, Jiude, and the various commanderies; the Inspector of Jiaozhou Du Hongwen raised his standard intending to attack him, but hearing there would be a replacement he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanjia, Yangmai ravaged Rinan and Jiude; the Jiaozhou inspector Du Hongwen mustered troops to punish him but halted when he learned he was to be replaced.

sentences.zh: 八年，又寇九德郡，入四會浦口。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again raided Jiude commandery, entering the mouth of Sihui harbor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he raided Jiude again and entered the mouth of Sihui harbor.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史阮彌之遣隊主相道生帥兵赴討，攻區栗城不克，乃引還。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jiaozhou Ruan Mizhi dispatched the company commander Xiang Daosheng leading troops to go punish him; attacking Quli city they did not overcome it, and therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaozhou inspector Ruan Mizhi sent company commander Xiang Daosheng to attack him; the assault on Quli city failed and the column withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十二年、十五年、十六年、十八年，每遣使貢獻，獻亦陋薄，而寇盜不已。

translations.literal: In the twelfth, fifteenth, sixteenth, and eighteenth years, each time he sent envoys with tribute, yet the tribute was also meager and shabby, while raiding and plunder did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth, fifteenth, sixteenth, and eighteenth years he sent tribute missions, but the gifts were paltry and his raids never stopped.

sentences.zh: 文帝忿其違傲，二十三年，使交州刺史檀和之、振武將軍宗愨伐之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was angry at his defiance and arrogance; in the twenty-third year he sent the Inspector of Jiaozhou Tan Hezhi and the Quelling Martial general Zong Que to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, enraged by his insolence, sent the Jiaozhou inspector Tan Hezhi and the Quelling Martial general Zong Que against him in the twenty-third year.

sentences.zh: 和之遣司馬蕭景憲為前鋒，陽邁聞之懼，欲輸金一萬斤、銀十萬斤、銅三十萬斤，還所略日南戶。

translations.literal: Hezhi dispatched the Major Xiao Jingxian as vanguard; Yangmai heard and was afraid, wishing to deliver ten thousand jin of gold, one hundred thousand jin of silver, and three hundred thousand jin of copper, and return the households plundered from Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi sent Major Xiao Jingxian as vanguard; Yangmai, alarmed, offered ten thousand jin of gold, one hundred thousand jin of silver, three hundred thousand jin of copper, and the Rinan households he had seized.

sentences.zh: 其大臣愺僧達諫止之。

translations.literal: His great minister Cao Sengda remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: His minister Cao Sengda dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 乃遣大帥范扶龍戍其北界區栗城。

translations.literal: He then dispatched the great commander Fan Fulong to garrison Quli city on his northern border.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he sent his great commander Fan Fulong to hold Quli city on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 景憲攻城克之，乘勝即克林邑，陽邁父子並挺身逃奔。

translations.literal: Jingxian attacked the city and overcame it; pressing the victory he immediately took Linyi, and Yangmai father and son both fled in person.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian stormed and took the city, then pressed on to capture Linyi while Yangmai and his son fled.

sentences.zh: 獲其珍異，皆是未名之寶。

translations.literal: They seized his rare and exotic goods, all treasures without names.
translations.idiomatic: They seized treasures so rare they had no names in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 又銷其金人，得黃金數十萬斤。

translations.literal: They also melted down his golden images and obtained several hundred thousand jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: They melted down his golden statues and recovered several hundred thousand jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 和之，高平金鄉人，檀憑之子也。

translations.literal: Hezhi was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping, son of Tan Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping and the son of Tan Ping.

sentences.zh: 以功封雲杜縣子。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yundu county.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yundu.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，為南兗州刺史，坐酣飲黷貨，迎獄中女子入內，免官禁錮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian he served as Inspector of Southern Yanzhou; for drunkenness, venal trafficking, and bringing a woman from prison into his inner quarters, he was dismissed from office and confined.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian he became inspector of Southern Yanzhou but was stripped of office and imprisoned for drunkenness, bribery, and keeping a woman from the jail in his quarters.

sentences.zh: 後病死，見胡神為祟。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness, having seen a foreign god as a malign spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness, claiming to be haunted by a foreign god.

sentences.zh: 追贈左將軍，諡曰襄子。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was awarded Left General and his posthumous title was Viscount Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted to Left General with the posthumous title Viscount Xiang.

sentences.zh: 孝武孝建二年，林邑又遣長史范龍跋奉使貢獻，除龍跋揚武將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, Linyi again sent Chief Clerk Fan Longba as envoy with tribute; Longba was appointed General Who Displays Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, Linyi again sent Chief Clerk Fan Longba with tribute, and Longba was appointed General Who Displays Martiality.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，林邑王范神成又遣長史范流奉表獻金銀器、香、布諸物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, King Fanshencheng of Linyi again sent Chief Clerk Fan Liu with a memorial presenting gold and silver vessels, incense, cloth, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming, King Fanshencheng of Linyi sent Chief Clerk Fan Liu with a memorial offering gold and silver vessels, incense, cloth, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰豫元年，又遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiyu under Emperor Ming, envoys were again sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiyu under Emperor Ming, Linyi again sent envoys with regional gifts.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，范文贊累遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: During Yongming of Qi, Fan Wenzan repeatedly sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming of Qi, Fan Wenzan repeatedly sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 梁天監九年，文贽子天凱奉獻白猴，詔加持節、督緣海諸軍事、威南將軍、林邑王。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianjian under Liang, the son of Wenzan, Tiankai, presented white monkeys; an edict made him Staff-Bearer, commander of all military affairs along the coast, General Who Awes the South, and King of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Tianjian under Liang, the son of Wenzan, Tiankai, presented white monkeys, and an edict invested him as Staff-Bearer, commander of all military affairs along the coast, General Who Awes the South, and King of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 死，子弼毳跋摩立，奉表貢獻。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Bicuibamo succeeded and presented memorials and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Bicuibamo succeeded and sent memorials and tribute.

sentences.zh: 普通七年，王高戍勝鎧遣使獻方物，詔以為持節、督緣海諸軍事、綏南將軍、林邑王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Putong, King Gaoshu Shengkai sent envoys offering local products; an edict made him Staff-Bearer, commander of all military affairs along the coast, General Who Pacifies the South, and King of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Putong, King Gaoshu Shengkai sent envoys with local products, and an edict invested him as Staff-Bearer, commander of all military affairs along the coast, General Who Pacifies the South, and King of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 大通元年，又遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, envoys were again sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong, tribute envoys were sent again.

sentences.zh: 大通二年，行林邑王高戍律陀羅跋摩遣使貢獻，詔以為持節、督緣海諸軍事、綏南將軍、林邑王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, Acting King of Linyi Gaoshu Lutuoluobamo sent envoys with tribute; an edict made him Staff-Bearer, commander of all military affairs along the coast, General Who Pacifies the South, and King of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong, Acting King of Linyi Gaoshu Lutuoluobamo sent tribute envoys, and an edict invested him as Staff-Bearer, commander of all military affairs along the coast, General Who Pacifies the South, and King of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 六年，又遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, envoys were again sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, envoys again brought local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 廣州諸山並狸獠，種類繁熾，前後屢為侵暴，曆世患之。

translations.literal: The various mountains of Guangzhou were all full of Li and Liao; their kinds were numerous and flourishing, and before and after they repeatedly committed invasions and outrages, a trouble through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: The hills of Guangzhou teemed with Li and Liao tribes whose numbers had swelled; generation after generation they raided the lowlands.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武大明中，合浦大帥陳檀歸順，拜龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the great commander of Hepu Chen Tan submitted and was appointed Dragon Cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the Hepu chieftain Chen Tan submitted and was appointed Dragon Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 檀乞官軍征討未附，乃以檀為高興太守，遣前朱提太守費沈、龍驤將軍武期南伐，並通朱崖道，並無功，輒殺檀而反，沈下獄死。

translations.literal: Tan requested government troops to campaign against those not yet submitted; they then made Tan Administrator of Gaoxing, dispatched the former Administrator of Zhuti Fei Shen and the Dragon Cavalry general Wu Qi south to attack, and also opened the Zhuya route; all achieved no merit; they then killed Tan and he rebelled; Shen was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tan asked for imperial troops to subdue holdouts and was made administrator of Gaoxing; the former Zhuti administrator Fei Shen and Dragon Cavalry General Wu Qi marched south and tried to open the Zhuya route, but the campaign failed, Tan was executed and rose in revolt, and Shen died in prison.

sentences.zh: 扶南國

translations.literal: The State of Funan
translations.idiomatic: The Kingdom of Funan

sentences.zh: 扶南國，在日南郡之南，海西大灣中，去日南可七千里。

translations.literal: The state of Funan lay south of Rinan commandery, in the great bay west of the sea, about seven thousand li from Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Funan lay south of Rinan commandery in the great gulf west of the sea, roughly seven thousand li from Rinan.

sentences.zh: 在林邑西南三千餘里。

translations.literal: It was more than three thousand li southwest of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: It stood more than three thousand li southwest of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 城去海五百里，有大江廣十里，從西流東入海。

translations.literal: The capital was five hundred li from the sea; there was a great river ten li wide flowing from west to east into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was five hundred li from the sea; a great river ten li wide ran west to east into the ocean.

sentences.zh: 其國廣輪三千餘里，土地洿下而平博，氣候風俗大較與林邑同。

translations.literal: That state's circumference was more than three thousand li; the land was low-lying, damp, and broad and flat; climate and customs were for the most part the same as Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom measured more than three thousand li around; the land was low, damp, and flat, and its climate and customs closely resembled those of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 出金、銀、銅、錫、沈木香、象、犀、孔翠、五色鸚鵡。

translations.literal: It produced gold, silver, copper, tin, agarwood, elephants, rhinoceroses, peafowl, and five-colored parrots.
translations.idiomatic: It exported gold, silver, copper, tin, agarwood, elephants, rhinoceros horn, peafowl, and multicolored parrots.

sentences.zh: 其南界三千餘里有頓遜國，在海崎上，地方千里。

translations.literal: On its southern border, more than three thousand li away, was the state of Dunsun, on a sea promontory, its territory a thousand li square.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand-odd li to the south lay Dunsun on a coastal headland, a kingdom a thousand li across.

sentences.zh: 城去海十里。

translations.literal: The capital was ten li from the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital stood ten li from the sea.

sentences.zh: 有五王，並羈屬扶南。

translations.literal: There were five kings, all bound and subordinate to Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Five kings ruled the realm, all in subordination to Funan.

sentences.zh: 頓遜之東界通交州諸賈人。

translations.literal: Dunsun's eastern frontier communicated with the merchants of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On its eastern border, Dunsun linked up with the merchants of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 其西界接天竺、安息徼外諸國，往還交易。

translations.literal: Its western frontier adjoined Tianzhu, Anxi, and the countries beyond the frontiers, going back and forth in trade.
translations.idiomatic: To the west it connected with India, Parthia, and the lands beyond the frontier, across which traders shuttled constantly.

sentences.zh: 其市東西交會，日有萬餘人。

translations.literal: At its markets east and west met; daily there were more than ten thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: Its bazaar was a crossroads where east and west converged, drawing more than ten thousand people each day.

sentences.zh: 珍物寶貨無不有，又有酒樹似安石榴，采其花汁停甕中，數日成酒。

translations.literal: Precious things and rare goods were not lacking; there was also a wine tree resembling the pomegranate—collecting its flower sap and setting it in jars, in several days it became wine.
translations.idiomatic: Every sort of treasure and luxury could be found there. There was even a wine tree that looked like a pomegranate: sap from its blossoms was collected in jars and fermented into wine within days.

sentences.zh: 頓遜之外大海洲中，又有毗騫國，去扶南八千里。

translations.literal: Beyond Dunsun, in an island of the great sea, there was also the state of Piqian, eight thousand li from Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Far beyond Dunsun, on a great island in the open sea, lay Piqian, eight thousand li from Funan.

sentences.zh: 傳其王身長丈二，頸長三尺，自古不死，莫知其年。

translations.literal: Tradition says its king's body was one zhang and two chi long, his neck three chi long; from antiquity he did not die, and none knew his age.
translations.idiomatic: Legend held that the king stood twelve feet tall with a neck three feet long, had never died since time immemorial, and whose age no one could tell.

sentences.zh: 王神聖，國中人善惡及將來事，王皆知之，是以無敢欺者。

translations.literal: The king was divine and holy; the people's good and evil and future affairs—the king knew them all, hence none dared to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: So holy was the king that he knew every deed and its consequence, and even what lay ahead—no one in the kingdom dared deceit.

sentences.zh: 南方號曰長頸王。

translations.literal: In the south they called him the Long-Neck King.
translations.idiomatic: Southerners knew him as the Long-Neck King.

sentences.zh: 國俗，有室屋衣服，噉粳米。

translations.literal: The customs of the state: there were houses, rooms, and clothing; they ate polished rice.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived in houses, wore clothes, and ate husked rice.

sentences.zh: 其人言語小異扶南。

translations.literal: The people's speech differed slightly from Funan's.
translations.idiomatic: Their language differed only slightly from that of Funan.

sentences.zh: 有山出金，金露生石上，無央限也。

translations.literal: There was a mountain producing gold; gold exposed and grew on the stones, without limit.
translations.idiomatic: A mountain yielded gold that formed openly on the rock face, in inexhaustible abundance.

sentences.zh: 國法，刑人並于王前噉其肉。

translations.literal: By state law, when punishing people, they all before the king ate his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: By law, condemned prisoners were executed before the king, who then ate their flesh.

sentences.zh: 國內不受估客，有往者亦殺而噉之，是以商旅不敢至。

translations.literal: Within the state they did not receive merchant-guests; any who went there were also killed and eaten, hence merchants and travelers did not dare to come.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants were not welcome: any who entered were killed and devoured, so traders kept well away.

sentences.zh: 王常樓居，不血食，不事鬼神。

translations.literal: The king constantly dwelled in a tower; he did not eat meat with blood, and did not serve ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The king lived in a tower, ate no meat, and worshipped no spirits.

sentences.zh: 其子孫生死如常人，唯王不死。

translations.literal: His descendants lived and died like ordinary people; only the king did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Only the king was immortal; his descendants lived and died like anyone else.

sentences.zh: 扶南王數使與書相報答。

translations.literal: The king of Funan repeatedly sent envoys with letters to exchange replies.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Funan and he often exchanged letters by envoy.

sentences.zh: 常遺扶南王純金五十人食器，形如圓盤，又如瓦塸，名為多羅，受五升，又如碗者受一升。

translations.literal: He regularly sent the king of Funan fifty men's worth of pure gold vessels, shaped like round plates and also like earthen jars, called duoluo, holding five sheng, and like bowls holding one sheng.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly sent the Funan king enough pure-gold tableware for fifty men—round platters and jar-shaped vessels called duoluo that held five sheng, and bowls holding one sheng.

sentences.zh: 王亦能作天竺書，書可三千言，說其宿命所由，與佛經相似，並論善事。

translations.literal: The king could also write Indian script; the writing was about three thousand words, explaining the causes of his past lives, similar to Buddhist scriptures, and all discussing good deeds.
translations.idiomatic: The king could even write in Indian script—a text of some three thousand characters explaining karmic origins, much like a sutra and devoted to the merits of virtue.

sentences.zh: 又傳扶南東界即大漲海，海中有大洲，洲上有諸薄國，國東有馬五洲。

translations.literal: Tradition also says Funan's eastern border was the great rising sea; in the sea there was a great isle; on the isle was the state of Zhubo; east of the state were five horse islands.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition placed Funan's eastern frontier at the open ocean, where a great island held the kingdom of Zhubo and, beyond it to the east, five isles called the Horse Isles.

sentences.zh: 復東行漲海千餘里，至自然大洲，其上有樹生火中，洲左近人剝取其皮，紡績作布，以為手巾，與蕉麻無異而色微青黑。

translations.literal: Continuing east through the rising sea more than a thousand li, one reached the Natural Great Isle; on it were trees growing amid fire; people near the left of the isle stripped their bark, spun and wove it into cloth, used as hand-towels, no different from plantain hemp but the color slightly bluish-black.
translations.idiomatic: Another thousand li east across the ocean lay the Isle of Natural Abundance, where flame-touched trees grew. Locals on the western shore stripped the bark, spun it into cloth for hand towels—much like hemp, but tinged bluish black.

sentences.zh: 若小垢洿，則投火中，復更精潔。

translations.literal: If there was a little dirt or stain, one cast it into the fire and it again became fine and clean.
translations.idiomatic: Minor stains could be burned away in fire, leaving the cloth fresh and clean again.

sentences.zh: 或作燈炷，用之不知盡。

translations.literal: Some made it into lamp wicks; used so, one did not know exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Wicks made from the same fiber seemed never to burn out.

sentences.zh: 扶南國俗本裸，文身被髮，不制衣裳，以女人為王，號曰柳葉。

translations.literal: Funan custom was originally nakedness, tattooed bodies and loose hair, not making garments; a woman was made king, titled Willow Leaf.
translations.idiomatic: Funan custom had once been bare skin, tattooed bodies, and loose hair with no proper clothes, and the ruler was a woman called Willow Leaf.

sentences.zh: 年少壯健，有似男子。

translations.literal: She was young, strong and robust, resembling a man.
translations.idiomatic: Young and powerfully built, she could pass for a man.

sentences.zh: 其南有激國，有事鬼神者字混填。

translations.literal: South of it was the state of Ji; one who served ghosts and spirits was named Hun Tian.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay the kingdom of Ji, where a spirit-worshipper named Kaundinya lived.

sentences.zh: 夢神賜之弓，乘賈人舶入海。

translations.literal: In a dream a spirit bestowed on him a bow; he boarded a merchant's ship and entered the sea.
translations.idiomatic: A god appeared in his dream and gave him a bow; he then boarded a merchant vessel and set out to sea.

sentences.zh: 混填晨起即詣廟，於神樹下得弓，便依夢乘舶入海，遂至扶南外邑。

translations.literal: Hun Tian rising early at once went to the temple; under the spirit tree he obtained the bow, then according to the dream boarded a ship and entered the sea, thus reaching an outer settlement of Funan.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Kaundinya went straight to the shrine, found the bow beneath the sacred tree, sailed as the dream had commanded, and landed at a Funan outpost.

sentences.zh: 柳葉人眾見舶至，欲劫取之。

translations.literal: Willow Leaf's people, many, seeing the ship arrive, wanted to plunder and seize it.
translations.idiomatic: When Willow Leaf's followers saw the ship approach, they moved to seize it by force.

sentences.zh: 混填即張弓射其舶，穿度一面，矢及侍者。

translations.literal: Hun Tian at once drew the bow and shot at their ship; the arrow pierced clear through one side; the arrow reached attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Kaundinya drew the bow and shot clear through the hull; the arrow struck one of Willow Leaf's attendants.

sentences.zh: 柳葉大懼，舉眾降混填，填乃教柳葉穿布貫頭，形不復露，遂君其國，納柳葉為妻，生子分王七邑。

translations.literal: Willow Leaf greatly feared; raising all the multitude she submitted to Hun Tian; Hun Tian then taught Willow Leaf to pierce cloth and pass it over the head, the form no longer exposed; thus he ruled the state, took Willow Leaf as wife, bore sons and divided seven settlements for them to rule.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Willow Leaf surrendered with all her people. Kaundinya taught them to wear cloth tunics pulled over the head so their bodies were covered; he then took the throne, married Willow Leaf, and appointed their sons as petty kings over seven districts.

sentences.zh: 其後王混盤況以詐力間諸邑，令相疑阻，因舉兵攻並之。

translations.literal: Later King Hun Pan Kuang by deceit and force estranged the various settlements, making them mutually suspicious and obstructive, then raised troops to attack and annex them.
translations.idiomatic: Later King Hun Pan Kuang used trickery and force to turn the districts against one another, then marched and conquered them one by one.

sentences.zh: 乃選子孫中分居諸邑，號曰小王。

translations.literal: Then he selected among descendants those to dwell separately in various settlements, titled Lesser Kings.
translations.idiomatic: He installed members of his line as Lesser Kings across the districts.

sentences.zh: 盤況年九十餘乃死，立中子盤盤，以國事委其大將范蔓。

translations.literal: Pan Kuang at more than ninety years then died; the middle son Pan Pan was enthroned; state affairs were entrusted to his great general Fan Man.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Kuang lived past ninety before he died. His middle son Pan Pan succeeded him and entrusted government to his general Fan Man.

sentences.zh: 盤盤立三年死，國人共舉蔓為王。

translations.literal: Pan Pan enthroned three years died; the people of the state together raised Man as king.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Pan reigned three years and died; the realm then raised Fan Man to the throne.

sentences.zh: 蔓勇健有權略，復以兵威攻伐旁國，咸服屬之，自號扶南大王。

translations.literal: Man was brave, strong, and had stratagems of authority; again by military might he attacked and punished neighboring states; all submitted and were attached to him; he styled himself Great King of Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Man was bold and shrewd. He subjugated the neighboring kingdoms by force and styled himself Great King of Funan.

sentences.zh: 乃作大船窮漲海，開國十餘，辟地五六千里。

translations.literal: Then he built great ships to exhaust the rising sea, opening more than ten states, opening land five or six thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: He built great ships to cross the ocean, founding more than ten states and extending his domain five or six thousand li.

sentences.zh: 次當伐金鄰國，蔓遇疾，遣太子金生代行。

translations.literal: Next he was about to campaign against the state of Jinlin; Man met with illness and sent the crown prince Jin Sheng to go in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to invade Jinlin, Fan Man fell ill and sent the crown prince Jin Sheng in his stead.

sentences.zh: 蔓姊子旃因篡蔓自立，遣人詐金生而殺之。

translations.literal: Man's elder sister's son Zhan thereupon usurped Man and enthroned himself; he sent men who deceived Jin Sheng and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Man's nephew Zhan seized the throne and had Jin Sheng lured to his death.

sentences.zh: 蔓死時有乳下兒名長在人間，至年二十，乃結國中壯士，襲殺旃。

translations.literal: When Man died there was an infant at the breast named Chang still among men; reaching age twenty, he then gathered strong men of the state and in a surprise attack killed Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Man left an infant named Chang, who at twenty rallied loyal warriors and killed Zhan in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 旃大將范尋又攻殺長而代立。

translations.literal: Zhan's great general Fan Xun again attacked and killed Chang and replaced him on the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's general Fan Xun then killed Chang and took the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 更繕國內，起觀閣遊戲之，朝旦中晡三四見客。

translations.literal: He again repaired the interior of the state, built towers and pavilions for recreation; at dawn, midday, and late afternoon three or four times he received guests.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the capital, erected towers and galleries for pleasure, and received visitors three or four times a day—at dawn, noon, and dusk.

sentences.zh: 百姓以蕉蔗龜鳥為禮。

translations.literal: The common people used plantains, sugar cane, turtles, and birds as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners brought gifts of plantains, sugar cane, turtles, and birds.

sentences.zh: 國法，無牢獄，有訟者，先齋三日，乃燒斧極赤，令訟者捧行七步。

translations.literal: By state law there were no prisons; when there were lawsuits, one first fasted three days, then burned an axe extremely red, and made the litigants carry it walking seven paces.
translations.idiomatic: There were no prisons. Litigants fasted three days, then a red-hot axe was placed in their hands and they were ordered to walk seven paces.

sentences.zh: 又以金鐶、雞卵投沸湯中，令探取之，若無實者手即爛，有理者則不。

translations.literal: Also gold rings and chicken eggs were cast into boiling water, and they were made to reach in and take them; if without truth the hand at once rotted; if with right reason then not.
translations.idiomatic: Accused parties also had to reach into boiling water for a gold ring or an egg; the hand of the guilty rotted away, but the innocent suffered no harm.

sentences.zh: 又於城溝中養鱷魚，門外圈猛獸，有罪者輒以餧猛獸及鱷魚，魚獸不食為無罪，三日乃放之。

translations.literal: Also in the city moat they raised crocodiles; outside the gate they penned fierce beasts; the guilty were then fed to fierce beasts and crocodiles; if fish and beasts did not eat them, it was guiltless; after three days they were released.
translations.idiomatic: Crocodiles were kept in the moat and wild beasts penned outside the gate. Criminals were thrown to them; if the animals refused the flesh after three days, the accused was deemed innocent and released.

sentences.zh: 鱷大者長三丈餘，狀似鼉，有四足，喙長六七尺，兩邊有齒利如刀劍，常食魚，遇得獐鹿及人亦噉之，蒼梧以南及外國皆有之。

translations.literal: Large crocodiles were more than three zhang long; their appearance resembled alligators; they had four feet; beaks six or seven chi long; on both sides teeth sharp as swords; they constantly ate fish; when they encountered deer and people they also devoured them; south of Cangwu and in foreign countries all had them.
translations.idiomatic: The largest crocodiles exceeded thirty feet, looked like alligators on four legs, with jaws six or seven feet long and teeth like blades. They fed mainly on fish but devoured deer and humans when they could. They were found south of Cangwu and throughout the southern lands.

sentences.zh: 吳時，遣中郎康泰、宣化從事朱應使于尋國，國人猶裸，唯婦人著貫頭。

translations.literal: In Wu times they dispatched Palace Gentleman Kang Tai and Assistant Director for Spreading Transformation Zhu Ying as envoys to Fan Xun's state; the people of the state were still naked; only women wore pierced-cloth head garments.
translations.idiomatic: During Wu, Palace Gentleman Kang Tai and Promotion Officer Zhu Ying were sent to Fan Xun's court. The people still went nearly naked; only women wore cloth pulled over the head.

sentences.zh: 泰、應謂曰：「國中實佳，但人褻露可怪耳。」

translations.literal: Tai and Ying said to him: "Within the state it is truly fine, but that people are indecently exposed is strange indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Kang Tai and Zhu Ying told him, "Your land is splendid, but it is odd that people go about so indecently exposed."

sentences.zh: 尋始令國內男子著橫幅。

translations.literal: Fan Xun then first ordered men within the state to wear horizontal cloth strips.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xun then ordered the men of the realm to wear loincloths.

sentences.zh: 橫幅，今幹漫也。

translations.literal: Horizontal cloth strips—today's ganman.
translations.idiomatic: These loincloths are what is now called a ganman.

sentences.zh: 大家乃截錦為之，貧者乃用布。

translations.literal: Great families then cut brocade to make them; the poor then used cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families cut theirs from brocade; the poor used plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康中，尋始遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: During the Taikang era of Emperor Wu of Jin, Fan Xun first sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taikang era of Emperor Wu of Jin, Fan Xun first sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 穆帝昇平元年，王竺旃檀奉表獻馴象，詔以勞費停之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengping under Emperor Mu, King Zhu Zhantan presented a memorial offering tame elephants; an edict ordered them stopped because of the labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengping under Emperor Mu, King Zhu Zhantan presented a memorial offering tame elephants; an edict ordered them stopped because of the labor and expense.

sentences.zh: 其後王憍陳如本天竺婆羅門也，有神語曰應王扶南。

translations.literal: The later king Jayavarman was originally a Brahman from India. A spirit spoke, saying he should rule Funan.
translations.idiomatic: The later king Jayavarman was originally a Brahman from India. A spirit spoke, saying he should rule Funan.

sentences.zh: 憍陳如心悅，南至盤盤。

translations.literal: Jayavarman was delighted and went south to Panpan.
translations.idiomatic: Jayavarman was delighted and went south to Panpan.

sentences.zh: 扶南人聞之，舉國欣戴，迎而立焉。

translations.literal: When the people of Funan heard of it, the whole country rejoiced and welcomed him, raising him to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Funan heard of it, the whole country rejoiced and welcomed him, raising him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 復改制度，用天竺法。

translations.literal: He again reformed the institutions and adopted Indian law.
translations.idiomatic: He again reformed the institutions and adopted Indian law.

sentences.zh: 憍陳如死，後王持災陀跋摩，宋文帝元嘉十一年、十二年、十五年，奉表獻方物。

translations.literal: When Jayavarman died, the later king Rudravarman, in the eleventh, twelfth, and fifteenth years of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, presented memorials offering local products.
translations.idiomatic: When Jayavarman died, the later king Rudravarman, in the eleventh, twelfth, and fifteenth years of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, presented memorials offering local products.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，王憍陳如闍邪跋摩遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: During Yongming of Qi, King Jayavarman Sheyebamo sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming of Qi, King Jayavarman Sheyebamo sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 梁天監二年，跋摩復遣使送珊瑚佛像，並獻方物，詔授安南將軍、扶南王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian under Liang, Bamo again sent envoys bringing a coral Buddha image together with local products; an edict invested him as General Who Pacifies the South and King of Funan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjian under Liang, Bamo again sent envoys bringing a coral Buddha image together with local products, and an edict invested him as General Who Pacifies the South and King of Funan.

sentences.zh: 其國人皆醜黑拳發，所居不穿井，數十家共一池引汲之。

translations.literal: The people of the state were all ugly, black, with curly hair; where they dwelled they did not dig wells; several tens of families shared one pool to draw and fetch water.
translations.idiomatic: The people were dark-skinned and curly-haired; they dug no wells, and dozens of households shared a single pond for water.

sentences.zh: 俗事天神，天神以銅為像，二面者四手，四面者八手，手各有所持。

translations.literal: Custom served the Celestial Spirit; the Celestial Spirit was cast in copper as images—those with two faces had four hands, those with four faces had eight hands; each hand held something different.
translations.idiomatic: They worshipped a celestial deity cast in bronze: two-faced images had four arms, four-faced images had eight, each hand gripping a different emblem.

sentences.zh: 或小兒，或鳥獸，或日月。

translations.literal: Sometimes a small child, sometimes birds and beasts, sometimes sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Some held a child, others a bird or beast, others the sun or moon.

sentences.zh: 其王出入乘象，嬪侍亦然。

translations.literal: The king going out and returning rode elephants; concubines and attendants likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The king traveled by elephant, as did his consorts and attendants.

sentences.zh: 王坐則偏踞翹膝，垂左膝至地，以白疊敷前，設金盆香爐於其上。

translations.literal: When the king sat he sat sideways crouching with raised knee, letting the left knee hang to the ground; white layered cloth was spread before him; a gold basin and incense burner were set upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Seated, the king rested one knee on the ground with the other raised, white cloth spread before him and a gold basin and incense burner set upon it.

sentences.zh: 國俗，居喪則剃除鬚髮。

translations.literal: State custom: in mourning residence one shaved off beard and hair.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning, they shaved head and beard.

sentences.zh: 死者有四葬：水葬則投之江流，火葬則焚為灰燼，土葬則瘞埋之，鳥葬則棄之中野。

translations.literal: The dead had four burials: water burial then cast into the river current; fire burial then burned to ashes; earth burial then buried in the ground; bird burial then abandoned in the open wild.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were disposed of in four ways: cast into rivers, cremated to ash, buried in earth, or left in the open for birds.

sentences.zh: 人性貪吝無禮義，男女恣其奔隨。

translations.literal: Human nature was greedy and stingy without ritual and righteousness; men and women followed their lustful pursuits at will.
translations.idiomatic: They were grasping and without propriety; men and women took lovers freely.

sentences.zh: 十年、十三年，跋摩累遣使貢獻，其年死。

translations.literal: In the tenth and thirteenth years, Bamo repeatedly sent envoys with tribute; that year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth and thirteenth years, Bamo repeatedly sent tribute envoys; that year he died.

sentences.zh: 庶子留陀跋摩殺其嫡弟自立。

translations.literal: His concubine-born son Liutuobamo killed his legitimate younger brother and set himself up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: His concubine-born son Liutuobamo killed his legitimate younger brother and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遣使竺當抱老奉表貢獻。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he sent the envoy Zhu Dangbaolao to present a memorial and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, he sent the envoy Zhu Dangbaolao with a memorial and tribute.

sentences.zh: 十八年，復遣使送天竺旃檀瑞像、婆羅樹葉；

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he again sent envoys bringing an auspicious sandalwood image from India and leaves of the bola tree;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, he again sent envoys bringing an auspicious sandalwood image from India and leaves of the bola tree;

sentences.zh: 並獻火齊珠，郁金、蘇合等香。

translations.literal: and also offered fire-jewel pearls, turmeric, storax, and other incenses.
translations.idiomatic: and also offered fire-jewel pearls, turmeric, storax, and other incenses.

sentences.zh: 普通元年、中大通二年、大同元年，累遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong, the second year of Zhongdatong, and the first year of Datong, he repeatedly sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putong, the second year of Zhongdatong, and the first year of Datong, he repeatedly sent envoys with local products.

sentences.zh: 五年，復遣使獻生犀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he again sent envoys to offer a live rhinoceros.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he again sent envoys offering a live rhinoceros.

sentences.zh: 又言其國有佛發，長一丈二尺。

translations.literal: He also said that his country had a hair of the Buddha, one zhang and two chi long.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that his kingdom possessed a hair of the Buddha twelve feet long.

sentences.zh: 詔遣沙門釋雲寶隨使往迎之。

translations.literal: An edict sent the monk Shi Yunbao to accompany the envoy and fetch it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched the monk Shi Yunbao to accompany the envoys and bring it back.

sentences.zh: 先是，三年八月，武帝改造阿育王佛塔，出舊塔下舍利及佛爪發，發青紺色，眾僧以手伸之，隨手長短，放之則旋屈為蠡形。

translations.literal: Before this, in the eighth month of the third year, Emperor Wu reconstructed the Ashoka Buddhist pagoda; from beneath the old pagoda emerged relics and the Buddha's nails and hair; the hair was bluish-indigo colored; the assembly of monks stretched it with the hand—it lengthened and shortened with the hand; released, it coiled spiraling into a spiral-shell shape.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the eighth month of the third year of his reign, Emperor Wu rebuilt the Ashoka pagoda. Beneath the old stupa lay relics together with the Buddha's nail-clippings and hair. The hair was deep blue-green; when monks pulled it, it stretched to whatever length they chose, and when released it coiled like a snail shell.

sentences.zh: 按僧伽經云：「佛發青而細，猶如藕莖絲。」

translations.literal: According to the Sengqie Sutra it says: "The Buddha's hair was bluish and fine, like lotus-stem filaments."
translations.idiomatic: The Sangha Sutra says: "The Buddha's hair was blue-green and fine as lotus-stem silk."

sentences.zh: 佛三昧經云：「我昔在宮沐頭，以尺量發，長一丈二尺。

translations.literal: The Buddha Samadhi Sutra says: "I formerly in the palace washed my head; measuring the hair with a ruler, it was one zhang and two chi long.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha Samadhi Sutra says: "When I lived in the palace and washed my hair, a ruler measured it at twelve feet.

sentences.zh: 放已右旋，還成蠡文。」

translations.literal: Released, it spiraled rightward, again forming a spiral-shell pattern."
translations.idiomatic: Released, it spiraled to the right and resumed its snail-shell curl."

sentences.zh: 則與帝所得同也。

translations.literal: Then it was the same as what the Emperor obtained.
translations.idiomatic: That matched exactly what the emperor had found.

sentences.zh: 阿育王即鐵輪王，王閻浮提一天下。

translations.literal: Ashoka was the Iron Wheel King; he ruled Jambudvipa and all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Ashoka was the universal Iron-Wheel King who ruled all of Jambudvipa.

sentences.zh: 佛滅度後，一日一夜，役鬼神造八萬四千塔，此即其一。

translations.literal: After the Buddha's nirvana, in one day and one night he employed ghosts and spirits to make eighty-four thousand pagodas; this was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: After the Buddha's nirvana, Ashoka commanded spirits to erect eighty-four thousand stupas in a single day and night; this was one of them.

sentences.zh: 吳時有尼居其地為小精舍，孫綝尋毀除之，塔亦同滅。

translations.literal: In Wu times a nun dwelt on that spot as a small refined lodge; Sun Chen soon destroyed and removed it; the pagoda likewise perished together.
translations.idiomatic: During Wu a nun had built a small monastery on the site; Sun Chen soon tore it down and the stupa disappeared with it.

sentences.zh: 吳平後，諸道人復于舊處建立焉。

translations.literal: After Wu was pacified, the various monks again at the old place established it.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Wu, monks rebuilt on the original ground.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝初度江，更修飾之。

translations.literal: When Jin Emperor Yuandi first crossed the Yangzi, he again repaired and adorned it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Jin first crossed the Yangzi, he restored and embellished it.

sentences.zh: 至簡文咸安中，使沙門安法程造小塔，未及成而亡。

translations.literal: Up to Emperor Jianwen's Xian'an era, he had the monk An Facheng build a small pagoda; before it was completed he died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xian'an reign of Emperor Jianwen, the monk An Facheng was commissioned to build a small stupa, but the emperor died before it was finished.

sentences.zh: 弟子僧顯繼而修立，至孝武太元九年，上金相輪及承露。

translations.literal: The disciple monk Xian continued and finished the building; up to Emperor Xiaowu's ninth year of Taiyuan, they added a gold dharmachakra wheel and finial basin.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Seng Xian completed the work; by the ninth year of the Taiyuan reign of Emperor Xiaowu, a gilded wheel and finial had been added.

sentences.zh: 其後，有西河離石縣胡人劉薩何遇疾暴亡，而心猶暖，其家未敢便殯，經七日更蘇。

translations.literal: After this, a foreigner of Lishi county in Xihe, Liu Sahe, met sudden death from illness; yet his heart was still warm; his family did not dare immediately bury him; after seven days he revived again.
translations.idiomatic: Later a man of foreign origin named Liu Sahe from Lishi in Xihe fell suddenly ill and died; his heart was still warm, so his family delayed burial—and after seven days he revived.

sentences.zh: 說云：「有兩吏見錄，向西北行，不測遠近。

translations.literal: He said: "Two clerks seeing me registered, toward the northwest we went; distant or near could not be measured.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Two underworld clerks seized me and led me northwest, I know not how far.

sentences.zh: 至十八地獄，隨報重輕，受諸楚毒。

translations.literal: Reaching the eighteen hells, according to retribution heavy or light, he suffered all tortures.
translations.idiomatic: I passed through the eighteen hells and suffered torments matching my deeds.

sentences.zh: 觀世音語云：'汝緣未盡，若得活可作沙門。

translations.literal: Guanshiyin spoke saying: 'Your affinity is not yet exhausted; if you obtain life you may become a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Guanyin said, "Your time has not yet come. If you live, become a monk.

sentences.zh: 洛下、齊城、丹陽、會稽並有阿育王塔，可往禮拜。

translations.literal: Luoyang, Qicheng, Danyang, and Kuaiji all have Ashoka pagodas; you may go to bow in worship.
translations.idiomatic: Ashoka stupas stand at Luoyang, Qicheng, Danyang, and Kuaiji—go worship at them.

sentences.zh: 若壽終則不墮地獄。

translations.literal: If when your lifespan ends you then will not fall into hell.
translations.idiomatic: When your life ends, you will not fall into hell.

sentences.zh: '」語竟如墜高岩，忽然醒寤。

translations.literal: ' When the words ended it was like falling from a high cliff; suddenly he awoke.
translations.idiomatic: When the words ended I seemed to plunge from a cliff and woke suddenly.""

sentences.zh: 因此出家名慧達。

translations.literal: Because of this he left home and was named Huida.
translations.idiomatic: He took vows and received the name Huida.

sentences.zh: 遊行禮塔，次至丹陽，未知塔處，及登越城四望，見長幹裏有異氣，因就禮拜，果是先阿育王塔所，屢放光明，由是定知必有舍利。

translations.literal: Traveling to worship at pagodas, next he reached Danyang, not knowing the pagoda's location; when he ascended Yue city's walls and looked four ways, he saw Changgan lane had an unusual aura; thereby he went to bow in worship; it truly was the site of the former Ashoka pagoda, repeatedly emitting light; from this he determined certainly there must be relics.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled worshipping at stupas and came to Danyang, unsure where this one stood. From atop Yue city he scanned the horizon and saw an uncanny radiance over Changgan Lane. He went to pay reverence and confirmed it as the site of the ancient Ashoka stupa, which had flashed with light again and again; he knew relics must lie below.

sentences.zh: 乃集眾就掘入一丈，得三石碑，並長六尺。

translations.literal: Then he gathered the multitude to dig; entering one zhang, they obtained three stone steles, each six chi long.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered a crowd to dig. One zhang down they uncovered three stone tablets, each six feet long.

sentences.zh: 中一碑有鐵函，函中有銀函，函中又有金函，盛三舍利及發爪各一枚，發長數尺。

translations.literal: In one stele was an iron casket; in the casket a silver casket; in the casket again a gold casket, holding three relics and one each of hair and nail-clippings; the hair was several chi long.
translations.idiomatic: One tablet enclosed an iron box, inside it a silver box, inside that a gold box holding three relics plus one hair and one nail-clipping—the hair several feet long.

sentences.zh: 即遷舍利近北對簡文所造塔西造一層塔。

translations.literal: Then they moved the relics northward; facing west of the pagoda made by Jianwen they built a one-story pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: The relics were moved north and a one-tier stupa was built just west of the stupa Emperor Jianwen had erected.

sentences.zh: 十六年，又使沙門僧尚加為三層。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, they again had the monk Seng Shang add to make three stories.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the monk Seng Shang was commissioned to raise it to three tiers.

sentences.zh: 即是武帝所開者也。

translations.literal: This was what Emperor Wu opened.
translations.idiomatic: This was the stupa Emperor Wu had opened.

sentences.zh: 初穿土四尺，得龍窟及昔人所舍金銀環釧釵鑷等諸雜寶物。

translations.literal: At first digging through earth four chi, they obtained a dragon cave and various mixed treasures that people of old had offered—gold and silver rings, bracelets, hairpins, tweezers, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: When digging began, four feet down they found a dragon's den and a trove of offerings—gold and silver rings, bracelets, pins, tweezers, and other treasures left by past donors.

sentences.zh: 可深九尺許至石磉，磉下有石函，函內有鐵壺以盛銀坩，坩內有金鏤罌盛三舍利如粟粒大，圓正光潔。

translations.literal: About nine chi deeper to the stone base; beneath the base was a stone casket; inside the casket an iron pot holding a silver dish; inside the dish a gold carved jar holding three relics like millet grains in size, round, upright, bright and smooth.
translations.idiomatic: Nine feet deeper lay a stone foundation; beneath it a stone casket holding an iron pot, inside that a silver dish, and within a gilded jar containing three relics the size of millet grains—perfect spheres, luminous and smooth.

sentences.zh: 函內有琉璃碗，碗內得四舍利及發爪。

translations.literal: Inside the casket was a glass bowl; inside the bowl they obtained four relics and nail-clippings and hair.
translations.idiomatic: A glass bowl in the casket held four more relics together with hair and nail-clippings.

sentences.zh: 爪有四枚，並為沈香色。

translations.literal: The nail-clippings were four pieces; all were agarwood in color.
translations.idiomatic: There were four nail-clippings, all the color of agarwood.

sentences.zh: 至其月二十七日，帝又到寺禮拜，設無礙大會，大赦。

translations.literal: Reaching the twenty-seventh day of that month, the Emperor again came to the temple to bow in worship, set up an unobstructed great assembly, and granted a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh of that month the emperor returned to worship at the temple, held a great dharma assembly, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 是日以金缽盛水泛舍利，其最小者隱不出，帝禮數十拜，舍利乃於缽內放光，旋回久之，乃當中而止。

translations.literal: That day with a gold bowl holding water they floated the relics; the smallest one hid and did not emerge; the Emperor bowed several tens of times; the relic then within the bowl emitted light, spinning round for a long time, then stopped in the center.
translations.idiomatic: That day relics were set afloat in a gold bowl of water. The smallest remained hidden until the emperor bowed dozens of times; then it shone from the bowl, wheeling in light for a long while before settling at the center.

sentences.zh: 帝問大僧正慧念曰：「見不可思議事不？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the Great Director of Monks Hui Nian: "Have you seen an inconceivable thing?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the chief monastic officer Hui Nian, "Have you witnessed anything beyond comprehension?"

sentences.zh: 慧念答曰：「法身常住，湛然不動。」

translations.literal: Hui Nian replied saying: "The Dharma-body eternally abides, deep and still, unmoving."
translations.idiomatic: Hui Nian answered, "The Dharma-body is ever-present, tranquil and unmoved."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「弟子欲請一舍利還台供養。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This disciple wishes to request one relic to take back to the palace for offerings and worship."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your disciple wishes to ask for one relic to take back to the palace for veneration."

sentences.zh: 至九月五日，又於寺設無礙大會，遣皇太子王侯朝貴等奉迎。

translations.literal: Reaching the fifth day of the ninth month, again at the temple they set up an unobstructed great assembly; they dispatched the crown prince, princes, nobles, and court dignitaries to escort and welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the ninth month another great assembly was held at the temple, and the crown prince, princes, nobles, and court officials were sent to escort the relic in procession.

sentences.zh: 是日風景明淨，傾都觀屬。

translations.literal: That day wind and scenery were bright and clear; the whole capital turned out to watch.
translations.idiomatic: The day was bright and clear, and the whole capital turned out to watch.

sentences.zh: 所設金銀供具等物，並留寺供養，並施錢一千萬為寺基業。

translations.literal: The gold and silver offering implements and such objects set out were all left at the temple for offerings; also he granted ten million coins as the temple's endowment foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The gold and silver ritual vessels were left at the temple for ongoing worship, and ten million coins were granted as the monastery's endowment.

sentences.zh: 至四年九月十五日，帝又至寺設無礙大會，豎二刹，各以金罌，次玉罌，重盛舍利及爪發內七寶塔內。

translations.literal: Reaching the fifteenth day of the ninth month of the fourth year, the Emperor again came to the temple and set up an unobstructed great assembly; he erected two pagodas, each with a gold jar, then a jade jar, again holding relics and nail-clippings and hair inside within a seven-jewels pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the ninth month in the fourth year the emperor returned for another great assembly and raised two stupas. In each, a gold vessel and then a jade vessel enclosed the relics, hair, and nail-clippings within jeweled pagodas.

sentences.zh: 又以石函盛寶塔，分入兩刹刹下，及王侯妃主百姓富室所舍金銀環釧等珍寶充積。

translations.literal: Also with stone caskets holding treasure pagodas, dividing and placing them under the two pagodas; and the gold and silver rings, bracelets, and such treasures offered by princes, consorts, princesses, common people, and wealthy households filled and piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Stone caskets holding the jeweled stupas were placed beneath the two towers, and the gold and silver rings, bracelets, and other treasures offered by princes, consorts, noblewomen, commoners, and the wealthy piled up beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 十一年十一月二日，寺僧又請帝於寺發般若經題。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on the second day of the eleventh month, the temple monks again invited the Emperor to the temple to expound the title of the Prajna Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the eleventh month in the eleventh year, the monks of the temple again invited the Emperor to the temple to open a lecture on the Prajna Sutra.

sentences.zh: 爾夕二塔俱放光明，敕鎮東邵陵王綸制寺大功德碑文。

translations.literal: That same evening both pagodas together emitted light. He ordered the Eastern Garrison Prince of Shaoling, Xiao Lun, to compose the great meritorious-deed stele inscription for the temple.
translations.idiomatic: That very night both pagodas shone with light at once, and the Emperor commanded Xiao Lun, Prince of Shaoling and commander of the eastern garrison, to write the stele inscription commemorating the temple's great acts of merit.

sentences.zh: 先是，二年改造會稽鄮縣塔，開舊塔中出舍利，遣光宅寺釋敬脫等四僧及舍人孫照暫迎還台。

translations.literal: Previously, in the second year, when the pagoda in Yin County, Kuaiji, was rebuilt, relics were found upon opening the old pagoda. He sent four monks including the monk Jingtuo of Guangzhai Temple and the palace attendant Sun Zhao to escort them temporarily back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the second year of the renovation of the pagoda at Yin County in Kuaiji, relics were discovered when the old stupa was opened. The Emperor dispatched four monks, among them Jingtuo of Guangzhai Temple, together with the palace attendant Sun Zhao to bring them briefly to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝禮拜竟，即送還縣，入新塔下，此縣塔亦是劉薩何所得也。

translations.literal: When the Emperor had finished paying homage, they were immediately sent back to the county and placed beneath the new pagoda. This county pagoda was also one obtained by Liu Sahe.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Emperor had finished his devotions, the relics were sent straight back to the county and enshrined beneath the new pagoda. This county stupa, too, was one that Liu Sahe had obtained.

sentences.zh: 晉咸和中，丹陽尹高悝行至張侯橋，見浦中五色光長數尺，不知何怪，乃令人於光處得金像，無有光趺。

translations.literal: During the Xianhe era of Jin, Gao Hui, intendant of Danyang, was traveling to Zhanghou Bridge when he saw in the inlet a five-colored light several chi long. Not knowing what marvel it was, he had men dig at the place of the light and found a gold image, but it had no shining halo or pedestal.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianhe era of Jin, Gao Hui, intendant of Danyang, was traveling to Zhanghou Bridge when he saw in the inlet a five-colored light several chi long. Not knowing what marvel it was, he had men dig where the light appeared and found a gold image, though it had no shining halo or pedestal.

sentences.zh: 悝乃下車載像還至長幹巷首，牛不肯進。

translations.literal: Hui then got down from his carriage, loaded the image, and returned to the head of Changgan Lane, but the ox refused to go forward.
translations.idiomatic: Hui got down from his carriage, loaded the image, and returned to the head of Changgan Lane, but the ox refused to go forward.

sentences.zh: 悝乃令馭人任牛所之，牛徑牽至寺，悝因留像付寺僧。

translations.literal: Hui then ordered the driver to let the ox go where it wished. The ox pulled straight to the temple, and Hui left the image with the temple monks.
translations.idiomatic: Hui ordered the driver to let the ox go where it wished. The ox pulled straight to the temple, and Hui left the image with the temple monks.

sentences.zh: 每至夜中，常放光明，又聞空中有金石之響。

translations.literal: Whenever night came, it would emit light, and sounds of metal and stone were also heard in the air.
translations.idiomatic: Each night it would shine with light, and sounds of metal and stone were heard in the air.

sentences.zh: 經一歲，臨海漁人張系世於海口忽見有銅花趺浮出，取送縣，縣人以送台，乃施像足，宛然合。

translations.literal: After a year, the fisherman Zhang Xishi of Linhai suddenly saw at the sea mouth a bronze lotus pedestal floating up. He took it and sent it to the county, and the county sent it to the capital; when it was set beneath the image's feet, it fit perfectly.
translations.idiomatic: After a year, the Linhai fisherman Zhang Xishi suddenly saw a bronze lotus pedestal floating up at the harbor mouth. He sent it to the county, and the county forwarded it to the capital; when it was set beneath the image's feet, it fit perfectly.

sentences.zh: 會簡文咸安元年，交州合浦人董宗之采珠沒水底，得佛光焰，交州送台，以施於像，又合焉。

translations.literal: Then, in the first year of Xian'an under Emperor Jianwen, Dong Zongzhi of Hepu in Jiaozhou was diving for pearls when he found a brilliant Buddha halo at the bottom. Jiaozhou sent it to the capital, and when it was attached to the image, it also fit.
translations.idiomatic: Then, in the first year of Xian'an under Emperor Jianwen, Dong Zongzhi of Hepu in Jiaozhou was diving for pearls when he found a brilliant Buddha halo underwater. Jiaozhou sent it to the capital, and when it was attached to the image, it also fit.

sentences.zh: 自咸和中得像，至咸安初，曆三十餘年，光趺始具。

translations.literal: From obtaining the image in the Xianhe era to the beginning of Xian'an, more than thirty years passed before the halo and pedestal were complete.
translations.idiomatic: From the discovery of the image in the Xianhe era to the beginning of Xian'an, more than thirty years passed before the halo and pedestal were complete.

sentences.zh: 初，高悝得像，後有西域胡僧五人來詣悝曰：「昔于天竺得阿育王造像，來至鄴下，逢胡亂，埋于河邊。

translations.literal: At first Gao Hui obtained the image. Later five foreign monks from the Western Regions came to Gao Hui and said: "Long ago in India we obtained an image made by King Ashoka. When we came to Ye, we encountered barbarian turmoil and buried it by the riverside.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Hui first came into possession of the image, five foreign monks from the Western Regions later came to see him and said, "In former days we obtained in India an image cast by King Ashoka. On our way to Ye we were caught in barbarian unrest and buried it beside a river.

sentences.zh: 今尋覓失所。」

translations.literal: Now we have searched for it but lost track of where it is."
translations.idiomatic: We have searched for it since, but cannot find where it lies."

sentences.zh: 五人嘗一夜俱夢見像曰：「已出江東，為高悝所得。」

translations.literal: The five men once, in a single night, all dreamed that the image said: "I have already emerged in Jiangdong and been obtained by Gao Hui."
translations.idiomatic: One night all five dreamed that the image spoke to them, saying, "I have already come forth in Jiangdong and been taken by Gao Hui."

sentences.zh: 悝乃送此五僧至寺，見像噓欷涕泣，像便放光，照燭殿宇。

translations.literal: Gao Hui then sent these five monks to the temple. When they saw the image they sobbed and wept, and the image immediately emitted light that illuminated the hall.
