translations.idiomatic: Gao Hui then brought the five monks to the temple. At the sight of the image they broke into sobs and tears, and the image at once radiated light that filled the hall with brilliance.

sentences.zh: 又瓦官寺慧邃欲摸寫像形，寺主僧尚慮損金色，謂邃曰：「若能令像放光，回身西向，乃可相許。」

translations.literal: Also, Huisui of Waguan Temple wished to make a rubbing copy of the image's form. The abbot, still worried it might damage the gilt, said to Huisui: "If you can make the image emit light and turn its body to face west, then I may grant permission."
translations.idiomatic: Huisui of Waguan Temple also wished to make a rubbing of the image, but the abbot, fearing the gilt might be harmed, told him, "Only if you can make the image shine with light and turn to face west will I give my consent."

sentences.zh: 慧邃便懇拜請。

translations.literal: Huisui at once earnestly bowed and prayed.
translations.idiomatic: Huisui immediately bowed in earnest supplication.

sentences.zh: 其夜像即轉坐放光，回身西向。

translations.literal: That same night the image immediately turned in its seat, emitted light, and turned its body to face west.
translations.idiomatic: That very night the image turned where it sat, radiated light, and shifted to face west.

sentences.zh: 明旦便許摸之。

translations.literal: At dawn permission was granted to make the rubbing.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the abbot allowed the rubbing to proceed.

sentences.zh: 像趺先有外國書，莫有識者，後有三藏那跋摩識之，雲是阿育王為第四女所造也。

translations.literal: On the image's pedestal there was formerly foreign script that no one could read. Later the Tripitaka master Napomo recognized it, saying it recorded that Ashoka had made it for his fourth daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign characters had long stood on the image's pedestal, but none could read them until the Tripitaka master Napomo deciphered them and declared that King Ashoka had commissioned the image for his fourth daughter.

sentences.zh: 及大同中，出舊塔舍利，敕市寺側數百家宅地以廣寺域，造諸堂殿並瑞像周回閣等，窮於輪奐焉。

translations.literal: During the Datong era, when relics were removed from the old pagoda, he ordered the purchase of several hundred households' residential land beside the temple to expand the temple grounds, and constructed various halls, the auspicious image, surrounding galleries, and the like—the splendor was taken to its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong period, when relics were taken from the old stupa, the Emperor ordered several hundred homes beside the temple bought up to enlarge the monastic precinct. Halls, the sacred image, encircling galleries, and more were built until the ornamentation reached its very limit.

sentences.zh: 其圖諸經變，並吳人張繇運手。

translations.literal: The paintings of various sutra transformation scenes were all executed by Zhang Yao of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: All the painted sutra tableaux were the work of Zhang Yao of Wu.

sentences.zh: 繇丹青之工，一時冠絕。

translations.literal: In the craft of painting, Zhang Yao at that time stood unrivaled.
translations.idiomatic: In his day Zhang Yao's mastery of brush and color had no equal.

sentences.zh: 訶羅陀國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Keroduo
translations.idiomatic: Keroduo

sentences.zh: 西南夷訶羅陀國，宋元嘉七年，遣使奉表曰：「伏承聖主信重三寶，興立塔寺，周滿世界。

translations.literal: The Southwestern Yi kingdom of Keroduo, in the seventh year of Yuanjia of Song, sent envoys presenting a memorial saying: "We humbly learn that the sage sovereign deeply believes in the Three Jewels, erecting pagodas and temples that fill the whole world.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanjia under the Song, the southwestern kingdom of Keroduo sent envoys with a memorial that read, "We humbly hear that Your Sacred Majesty holds the Three Jewels in deep reverence and raises pagodas and temples until they fill the world.

sentences.zh: 今故遣使二人，表此微心。」

translations.literal: We therefore now send two envoys to express this humble sentiment."
translations.idiomatic: We therefore send two envoys to convey this modest devotion."

sentences.zh: 呵羅單國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Heluodan
translations.idiomatic: Heluodan

sentences.zh: 呵羅單國都闍婆洲，元嘉七年，遣使獻金剛指環、赤鸚鵡鳥、天竺國白疊、古貝、葉波國古貝等物。

translations.literal: The kingdom of Heluodan is situated in Java. In the seventh year of Yuanjia it sent envoys presenting a diamond ring, red parrots, white cotton cloth from India, kapok cloth, kapok from Yeyabo, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: Heluodan lay in Java. In the seventh year of Yuanjia its envoys brought tribute of a diamond ring, crimson parrots, white cotton from India, kapok cloth, kapok from Yeyabo, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 十年，呵羅單國王毗沙跋摩奉表曰：「常勝天子陛下，諸佛世尊，常樂安隱，三達六通，為世間導，是名如來，是故至誠五體敬禮。」

translations.literal: In the tenth year, King Vishavarman of Heluodan presented a memorial saying: "To His Majesty the Ever-Victorious Son of Heaven—the World-Honored Ones of all Buddhas, ever dwelling in bliss and tranquility, possessed of the three penetrations and six supernormal powers, guides of the world—this is what is called the Tathagata. Therefore with utmost sincerity I prostrate in veneration with my whole body."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year King Vishavarman of Heluodan submitted a memorial that began, "To His Majesty the Ever-Victorious Son of Heaven: the World-Honored Buddhas abide forever in bliss and peace, endowed with the three penetrations and six supernormal powers, guiding the world—this is the Tathagata. With utmost sincerity I bow in full prostration."

sentences.zh: 其後為子所篡奪。

translations.literal: Afterward he was usurped by his son.
translations.idiomatic: He was later overthrown by his own son.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又上表。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he again submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year another memorial was sent.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，文帝詔曰：「呵羅單、婆皇、婆達三國，頻越遐海，款化納貢，遠誠宜甄，可並加除授。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Emperor Wen issued an edict saying: "The three kingdoms of Heluodan, Pohuang, and Pada have repeatedly crossed the distant seas, sincerely submitted to our transforming influence, and presented tribute. Their distant sincerity deserves recognition; all may concurrently be granted official appointments."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year Emperor Wen decreed, "Heluodan, Pohuang, and Pada have again and again crossed the far seas, drawn near in submission, and offered tribute. Such distant loyalty deserves reward; let them all be granted official titles at once."

sentences.zh: 乃遣使策命之。

translations.literal: Envoys were then dispatched to invest them with offices by formal patent.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to invest them by formal patent.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，又遣長史婆和沙彌獻方物。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the chief clerk Pohe and the shramana were again sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year the chief clerk Pohe and a shramana envoy again brought local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 婆皇國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Pohuang
translations.idiomatic: Pohuang

sentences.zh: 婆皇國，元嘉二十六年，國王舍利婆羅跋摩遣使獻方物四十一種，文帝策命之為婆皇國王。

translations.literal: The kingdom of Pohuang—in the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, King Shilipoluobamo sent envoys presenting forty-one kinds of local products, and Emperor Wen invested him as King of Pohuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia King Shilipoluobamo of Pohuang sent envoys bearing forty-one kinds of local goods, and Emperor Wen invested him as king of Pohuang.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，復遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year envoys were again sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year tribute envoys came again.

sentences.zh: 孝武孝建三年，又遣長史竺那婆智奉表獻方物，以那婆智為振威將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, the chief clerk Zhunabozhi was again sent presenting a memorial and local products; Zhunabozhi was appointed General Who Pacifies Might.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu the chief clerk Zhunabozhi arrived with a memorial and local products, and Zhunabozhi was named General Who Pacifies Might.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，獻赤白鸚鵡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming, red and white parrots were presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daming crimson and white parrots were sent as tribute.

sentences.zh: 大明八年、明帝泰始二年，又遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daming and the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming, envoys were again sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Daming and again in the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming, tribute envoys were dispatched.

sentences.zh: 明帝以其長史竺須羅達、前長史振威將軍竺那婆智並為龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming made both their chief clerk Zhuxuluoda and the former chief clerk, General Who Pacifies Might Zhunabozhi, Generals of Ferocious Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming appointed both their chief clerk Zhuxuluoda and the former chief clerk and General Who Pacifies Might, Zhunabozhi, as Generals of Ferocious Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 婆達國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Pada
translations.idiomatic: Pada

sentences.zh: 婆達國，元嘉二十六年，國王舍利不陵伽跋摩遣使獻方物，文帝策命之為婆達國王。

translations.literal: The kingdom of Pada—in the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, King Shilibulingjiabamo sent envoys presenting local products, and Emperor Wen invested him as King of Pada.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia King Shilibulingjiabamo of Pada sent envoys with local products, and Emperor Wen invested him as king of Pada.

sentences.zh: 二十六年、二十八年，復遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth and twenty-eighth years envoys were again sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth and twenty-eighth years envoys again brought local products.

sentences.zh: 闍婆達國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Zhebaduo
translations.idiomatic: Zhebaduo

sentences.zh: 闍婆達國，元嘉十二年，國王師黎婆達呵陀羅跋摩遣使奉表曰：「宋國大主大吉天子足下，教化一切，種智安隱，天人師降伏四魔，成等正覺，轉尊法輪，度脫眾生。

translations.literal: The kingdom of Zhebaduo—in the twelfth year of Yuanjia, King Shilipodahituoluobamo sent envoys presenting a memorial saying: "At the feet of the Great Lord, the Greatly Auspicious Son of Heaven of Song—who transforms all beings, whose seed-wisdom brings peace and tranquility, the Teacher of gods and humans who subdues the four maras, who has attained perfect enlightenment, who turns the honored wheel of the Law, and who delivers and liberates all living beings—
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia King Shilipodahituoluobamo of Zhebaduo sent envoys with a memorial addressed, "At the feet of the Great Lord, the Greatly Auspicious Son of Heaven of Song: You transform all beings; Your seed-wisdom brings peace and ease; as Teacher of gods and men You subdue the four maras, attain perfect enlightenment, turn the honored Wheel of the Law, and deliver all living beings—

sentences.zh: 我雖在遠，亦沾靈潤。」

translations.literal: though I dwell far away, I too am touched by Your sacred grace."
translations.idiomatic: though I dwell far away, I too am touched by Your sacred grace."

sentences.zh: 盤盤國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Panpan
translations.idiomatic: Panpan

sentences.zh: 盤盤國，元嘉、孝建、大明中，並遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: The kingdom of Panpan—during Yuanjia, Xiaojian, and Daming it repeatedly sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Panpan sent tribute envoys throughout the Yuanjia, Xiaojian, and Daming reigns.

sentences.zh: 梁中大通元年、四年，其王使使奉表累送佛牙及畫塔，並獻沈檀等香數十種。

translations.literal: In the first and fourth years of Zhongdatong under Liang, its king's envoys repeatedly sent memorials, bringing Buddha's tooth relics and painted pagodas, and presenting dozens of varieties of agarwood and other incense.
translations.idiomatic: In the first and fourth years of Zhongdatong under Liang its king's envoys repeatedly sent memorials, bearing Buddha's tooth relic and painted stupa images together with several dozen kinds of agarwood and other incense.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，復遣使送菩提國舍利及畫塔圖，並菩提樹葉、詹糖等香。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year envoys were again sent bringing relics from the land of Bodhi, painted pagoda images, bodhi-tree leaves, ghanosugar incense, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth year envoys came again with relics from the land of Bodhi, painted stupa images, bodhi leaves, ghanosugar incense, and other fragrant goods.

sentences.zh: 丹丹國，中大通三年，其王遣使奉表送牙像及畫塔二軀，並獻火齊珠、古貝、雜香藥。

translations.literal: The kingdom of Dandan—in the third year of Zhongdatong, its king sent envoys presenting a memorial and offering ivory images and two painted pagodas, together with fire-jewel pearls, kapok cloth, and assorted fragrant medicines.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongdatong, the king of Dandan sent envoys with a memorial offering ivory images and two painted stupas, together with fire-jewel pearls, kapok cloth, and assorted fragrant medicines.

sentences.zh: 大同元年，復遣使獻金銀、琉璃、雜寶、香藥等物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, envoys were again sent presenting gold, silver, glass, assorted treasures, fragrant medicines, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong, envoys again brought gold, silver, glass, assorted treasures, fragrant medicines, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 幹陀利國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Gantoli
translations.idiomatic: Gantoli

sentences.zh: 幹陀利國，在南海洲上，其俗與林邑、扶南略同，出斑布、古貝、檳榔。

translations.literal: The kingdom of Gantoli is on an island in the Southern Sea. Its customs are roughly the same as those of Linyi and Funan. It produces patterned cloth, kapok, and betel nuts.
translations.idiomatic: Gantoli lay on an island in the Southern Sea. Its ways resembled those of Linyi and Funan, and it produced patterned cloth, kapok, and betel nut.

sentences.zh: 檳榔特精好，為諸國之極，宋孝武世，王釋婆羅那鄰陀遣長史竺留陀獻金銀寶器。

translations.literal: Its betel nuts are especially fine, the best among all kingdoms. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, King Shiboluanalintuo sent the chief clerk Zhuliutuo presenting gold, silver, and precious vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Its betel nuts were exceptionally fine—the finest in any kingdom. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, King Shiboluanalintuo sent his chief clerk Zhuliutuo with gold, silver, and precious vessels.

sentences.zh: 梁天監元年，其王瞿曇修跋陀羅以四月八日夢一僧謂曰：「中國今有聖主，十年之後，佛法大興。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian under Liang, on the eighth day of the fourth month its king Gautama Xiubatuoluo dreamed of a monk who said to him: "China now has a sage sovereign. Ten years hence the Buddhist Law will flourish greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian under Liang, on the eighth day of the fourth month King Gautama Xiubatuoluo dreamed of a monk who told him, "China now has a sage ruler. Ten years from now the Buddhist Law will flourish greatly.

sentences.zh: 汝若遣使貢奉禮敬，則土地豐樂，商旅百倍；

translations.literal: If you send envoys to present tribute and pay respects, your land will be rich and joyous, and merchants and travelers will increase a hundredfold;
translations.idiomatic: If you send envoys to offer tribute and pay homage, your land will grow rich and content, and merchants and travelers will multiply a hundredfold;

sentences.zh: 若不信我，則境土不得自安。」

translations.literal: If you do not believe me, your territory will know no peace."
translations.idiomatic: but if you do not believe me, your realm will know no peace."

sentences.zh: 初未之信，既而又夢此僧曰：「汝若不信我，當與汝往觀。」

translations.literal: At first he did not believe it. Then he dreamed again of this monk, who said: "If you do not believe me, I shall take you to go and see for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: At first he did not believe it. Then he dreamed of the monk again, who said, "If you still do not believe me, I shall take you to see for yourself."

sentences.zh: 乃於夢中至中國拜覲天子。

translations.literal: In his dream he then came to China and paid obeisance to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the dream he traveled to China and bowed before the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 既覺心異之，陀羅本工畫，乃寫夢中所見武帝容質，飾以丹青，仍遣使並畫工奉表獻玉盤等物。

translations.literal: When he awoke his heart was struck by wonder. Batuo was himself skilled at painting, so he painted the appearance of Emperor Wu as he had seen him in the dream, adorned it with colors, and still sent envoys together with painters presenting a memorial and gifts such as a jade tray.
translations.idiomatic: When he awoke he was deeply moved. Batuo was himself a skilled painter, so he painted Emperor Wu's features as he had seen them in the dream, colored the portrait, and sent envoys together with painters bearing a memorial and gifts that included a jade tray.

sentences.zh: 使人既至，摸寫帝形以還其國，比本畫則符同焉。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived, they made a rubbing copy of the Emperor's likeness to take back to their kingdom; compared with the original painting it matched exactly.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys reached the capital they made a copy of the Emperor's likeness to carry home, and it matched the original painting exactly.

sentences.zh: 因盛以寶函，日加敬禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was enshrined in a precious casket, and daily reverence was added.
translations.idiomatic: The portrait was then placed in a jeweled casket and honored with daily worship.

sentences.zh: 後跋陀死，子毗針邪跋摩立，十七年，遣長史毗員跋摩奉表獻金芙蓉、雜香藥等。

translations.literal: Later Batuo died and his son Pizhenyebamo succeeded. In the seventeenth year the chief clerk Piyuanbamo was sent presenting a memorial with golden lotus flowers, assorted fragrant medicines, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: After Batuo's death his son Pizhenyebamo succeeded him. In the seventeenth year the chief clerk Piyuanbamo was sent with a memorial and tribute of golden lotus blossoms, assorted fragrant medicines, and more.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，復遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong envoys were again sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putong tribute envoys came again with local products.

sentences.zh: 狼牙修國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Langyaxiu
translations.idiomatic: Langyaxiu

sentences.zh: 狼牙修國，在南海中。

translations.literal: The kingdom of Langyaxiu is in the Southern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Langyaxiu lay in the Southern Sea.

sentences.zh: 其界東西三十日行，南北二十日行，北去廣州二萬四千里。

translations.literal: Its territory extends thirty days' travel east to west and twenty days' travel north to south. It lies twenty-four thousand li north of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its borders ran thirty days' journey east to west and twenty days' journey north to south, twenty-four thousand li north of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 土氣物產與扶南略同，偏多棧、沈、婆律香等。

translations.literal: Its climate and products are roughly the same as Funan's, but it has especially more agarwood, aloeswood, and vara incense.
translations.idiomatic: Its climate and products resembled Funan's, though it had especially abundant agarwood, aloeswood, and vara incense.

sentences.zh: 其俗，男女皆袒而被髮，以古貝為幹漫，其王及貴臣乃加雲霞布覆胛，以金繩為絡帶，金環貫耳。

translations.literal: Its custom: men and women alike go bare-chested with hair worn loose, using kapok as a lower garment. The king and noble officials additionally drape cloud-and-mist cloth over the shoulders, use gold cords as girdle-belts, and wear gold rings through their ears.
translations.idiomatic: By custom men and women alike went bare-chested with loose hair, wearing kapok as a lower garment. The king and nobles added cloud-patterned cloth over the shoulders, girded themselves with gold cords, and wore gold rings in their ears.

sentences.zh: 女子則被布，以瓔珞繞身。

translations.literal: Women wrap themselves in cloth and wear strings of jewels around their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Women wrapped themselves in cloth and wound strings of jewels about their bodies.

sentences.zh: 其國累磚為城，重門樓閣。

translations.literal: The country builds its walls of stacked brick, with layered gates, towers, and pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom built its walls of stacked brick, with layered gates, towers, and galleries.

sentences.zh: 王出乘象，有幡旄旗鼓，罩白蓋，兵衛甚嚴。

translations.literal: When the king goes out he rides an elephant carriage, with banners, pennants, flags, and drums, shaded by a white canopy; his armed guard is very strict.
translations.idiomatic: When the king went abroad he rode an elephant, accompanied by banners, pennants, flags, and drums beneath a white canopy, with a stern armed escort.

sentences.zh: 國人說，立國以來四百餘年，後嗣衰弱，王族有賢者，國人歸向之。

translations.literal: The people of the country say that since the founding of the state more than four hundred years have passed. Later the royal line grew weak, and there was a worthy man among the royal clan toward whom the people turned.
translations.idiomatic: The people said that more than four hundred years had passed since the kingdom was founded. In time the royal line weakened, and the people turned toward a worthy man of the royal clan.

sentences.zh: 王聞乃加囚執，其鎖無故自斷。

translations.literal: When the king heard of this he had him put in chains and imprisoned, but the fetters broke for no reason.
translations.idiomatic: When the king heard of this he had the man bound and imprisoned, but the shackles broke of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 王以為神，因不敢害，乃逐出境，遂奔天竺。

translations.literal: The king took this for divine power and therefore dared not harm him; instead he expelled him from the country, and he fled to India.
translations.idiomatic: The king took this as a sign of the divine and dared not harm him, but drove him from the realm instead. The man fled to India.

sentences.zh: 天竺妻以長女。

translations.literal: India gave him its eldest daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: India gave him its eldest daughter as wife.

sentences.zh: 俄而狼牙王死，大臣迎還為王。

translations.literal: Before long the king of Langya died, and the ministers welcomed him back to become king.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the king of Langya died, and the ministers welcomed the exile back to rule.

sentences.zh: 二十餘年死，子婆伽達多立。

translations.literal: After more than twenty years he died, and his son Baguaduo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty years on the throne he died, and his son Baguaduo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 天監十四年，遣使阿撤多奉表。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianjian he sent the envoy Acheduo presenting a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianjian he sent the envoy Acheduo with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 婆利國

translations.literal: The Kingdom of Bali
translations.idiomatic: Bali

sentences.zh: 婆利國，在廣州東南海中洲上，去廣州二月日行。

translations.literal: The kingdom of Bali is on an island in the sea southeast of Guangzhou, two months' travel from Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bali lay on an island in the sea southeast of Guangzhou, two months' voyage from the port.

sentences.zh: 國界東西五十日行，南北二十日行。

translations.literal: The kingdom's borders run fifty days' travel east to west and twenty days' travel north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Its borders extended fifty days' journey east to west and twenty days' journey north to south.

sentences.zh: 有一百三十六聚。

translations.literal: There are one hundred thirty-six settlements.
translations.idiomatic: It contained one hundred thirty-six settlements.

sentences.zh: 土氣暑熱，如中國之盛夏。

translations.literal: The climate is hot and humid, like midsummer in China.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was sweltering, like midsummer in China.

sentences.zh: 穀一歲再熟，草木常榮。

translations.literal: Grain ripens twice a year; plants and trees are evergreen.
translations.idiomatic: Grain ripened twice a year, and plants and trees stayed green through the seasons.

sentences.zh: 海出文螺、紫貝。

translations.literal: The sea yields ornamental conches and purple cowries.
translations.idiomatic: The sea yielded ornamental conches and purple cowries.

sentences.zh: 有石名坩貝羅，初采之柔軟，及刻削為物暴幹之，遂大硬。

translations.literal: There is a stone called ganbeiluo: when first quarried it is soft, but once carved into objects and sun-dried it becomes very hard.
translations.idiomatic: There was a stone called ganbeiluo that was soft when first taken from the quarry, but once carved and sun-dried it grew very hard.

sentences.zh: 其國人披古貝如帊，及為都縵。

translations.literal: The people of the country wear kapok like a cloak, and also use it as turbans.
translations.idiomatic: The people wore kapok like cloaks and wrapped it as turbans.

sentences.zh: 王乃用斑絲者，以瓔珞繞身，頭著金冠高尺餘，形如弁，綴以七寶之飾。

translations.literal: The king alone uses patterned silk. Jeweled strings wind around his body. On his head he wears a gold crown more than a foot high, shaped like a cap, adorned with the seven treasures.
translations.idiomatic: The king alone wore patterned silk, with jeweled strings wound about his body. On his head he wore a gold crown more than a foot high, shaped like an official cap and set with the seven treasures.

sentences.zh: 帶金裝劍，偏坐金高坐，以銀蹬支足。

translations.literal: He wears a sword with gold fittings, sits sideways on a lofty golden seat, and rests his feet on silver stirrups.
translations.idiomatic: He girded on a sword with gold fittings, sat sideways upon a high golden seat, and rested his feet on silver stirrups.

sentences.zh: 侍女皆為金花雜寶之飾，或持白毦拂及孔雀扇。

translations.literal: The attending maidens are all adorned with golden flowers and assorted jewels, some holding white yak-tail whisks and peacock-feather fans.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant maidens were adorned with golden flowers and assorted jewels, some bearing white yak-tail whisks and peacock-feather fans.

sentences.zh: 王出以象駕輿，輿以雜香為之，上施羽蓋、珠簾。

translations.literal: When the king goes out he rides in an elephant-drawn carriage; the carriage is made of mixed incense, topped with a feather canopy and pearl curtains.
translations.idiomatic: When the king went abroad he rode in an elephant-drawn carriage built of blended incense, topped with a feather canopy and pearl curtains.

sentences.zh: 其導從吹螺擊鼓。

translations.literal: His escort blow conch shells and beat drums.
translations.idiomatic: His escort blew conch shells and beat drums.

sentences.zh: 王姓憍陳如，自古未通中國，問其先及年數不能記。

translations.literal: The royal surname is Kaundinya. Since antiquity they had no contact with China; asked about their ancestry and the years of their history, they could not say.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house bore the surname Kaundinya. From antiquity they had had no contact with China, and when asked about their origins and the length of their history they could not say.

sentences.zh: 自言白淨王夫人即其國女。

translations.literal: They say themselves that the consort of King Suddhodana was a woman of their country.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed that the consort of King Suddhodana had been a woman of their land.

sentences.zh: 天監十六年，遣使奉表獻金席等。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Tianjian envoys were sent presenting a memorial and offering golden mats and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Tianjian envoys arrived with a memorial and tribute that included golden mats.

sentences.zh: 普通三年，其王頻伽復遣使珠智獻白鸚鵡、青蟲、兜鍪、琉璃器、古貝、螺杯、雜香藥等數十種。

translations.literal: In the third year of Putong its king Pinjia again sent the envoy Zhuzhi presenting white parrots, green insects, helmets, glassware, kapok cloth, conch-shell cups, assorted fragrant medicines, and dozens of other items.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Putong King Pinjia again sent the envoy Zhuzhi with white parrots, green beetles, helmets, glassware, kapok cloth, conch-shell cups, assorted fragrant medicines, and several dozen other goods.

sentences.zh: 中天竺國

translations.literal: Central India
translations.idiomatic: Central India

sentences.zh: 中天竺國，在大月支東南數千里，地方三萬里，一名身毒。

translations.literal: Central India lies several thousand li southeast of the Great Yuezhi. Its territory covers thirty thousand li; it is also called Shendu.
translations.idiomatic: Central India lay several thousand li southeast of the Great Yuezhi. Its domain covered thirty thousand li, and it was also known as Shendu.

sentences.zh: 漢世張騫使大夏，見邛竹杖、蜀布，國人云市之身毒，即天竺也。

translations.literal: In Han times when Zhang Qian was envoy to Daxia, he saw Qiong bamboo staffs and Shu cloth; the people of that country said they were purchased in Shendu—that is, Tianzhu (India).
translations.idiomatic: In Han times, when Zhang Qian went as envoy to Daxia, he saw Qiong bamboo staffs and Shu cloth. The people there said such goods were bought in Shendu—that is, in India.

sentences.zh: 從月支、高附西，南至西海，東至盤越，列國數十，每國置王，其名雖異，皆身毒也。

translations.literal: From the Yuezhi and Gaofu westward, south to the Western Sea and east to Panyue, there are several dozen separate states, each with its own king. Though their names differ, all are Shendu.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yuezhi and Gaofu in the west to the Western Sea in the south and Panyue in the east lay several dozen states, each with its own king. Their names differed, but all were part of Shendu.

sentences.zh: 漢時羈屬月支。

translations.literal: In Han times they were subordinate to the Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times they were subject to the Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 其俗土著與月支同，而卑濕暑熱，人畏戰，弱于月支。

translations.literal: Their custom is to dwell sedentarily as the Yuezhi do, but the land is low, damp, and hot; the people fear warfare and are weaker than the Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Like the Yuezhi they were settled agriculturalists, but the land was low, damp, and hot. The people feared war and were weaker than the Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 國臨大江，名新陶，源出昆侖。

translations.literal: The country borders a great river called Xintao, which rises in Kunlun.
translations.idiomatic: The country bordered a great river called Xintao, which had its source in Kunlun.

sentences.zh: 分為五江，總名恒水。

translations.literal: It divides into five streams; collectively they are called the Ganges.
translations.idiomatic: It divided into five branches, known together as the Ganges.

sentences.zh: 其水甘美，下有真鹽，色正白如水精。

translations.literal: Its waters are sweet and fine. Beneath them lies true salt, pure white in color like crystal.
translations.idiomatic: Its waters were sweet and pure. True salt lay beneath them, white as crystal.

sentences.zh: 土出犀、象、貂鼠、玳瑁、火齊、金銀銅鐵、金縷織成金罽、細靡白疊、好裘、毾憕。

translations.literal: The soil yields rhinoceros, elephants, sable martens, tortoiseshell, fire crystal, gold, silver, copper, and iron; gold-thread brocade woven into gold kasaya cloth, fine soft white layered cloth, fine furs, and carpets.
translations.idiomatic: The land produced rhinoceros horn, elephants, sable, tortoiseshell, fire crystal, gold, silver, copper, and iron, along with gold-thread brocade woven into gold kasaya cloth, fine white layered textiles, good furs, and carpets.

sentences.zh: 火齊狀如雲母，色如紫金，有光曜，別之則薄如蟬翼，積之則如紗縠之重遝也。

translations.literal: Fire crystal is shaped like mica; its color is like purple gold, and it has a bright luster. Split apart it is thin as a cicada's wing; piled up it is like gauze silk folded in layers.
translations.idiomatic: Fire crystal resembled mica in form and purple gold in color, with a bright luster. Split apart, it was as thin as a cicada's wing; piled up, it lay in layers like folded gauze.

sentences.zh: 西與大秦、安息交市海中。

translations.literal: To the west they trade on the sea with Daqin and Parthia.
translations.idiomatic: To the west they traded by sea with Daqin and Parthia.

sentences.zh: 多大秦珍物，珊瑚、琥珀、金碧、珠璣、琅玕、郁金、蘇合。

translations.literal: There are many precious things from Daqin: coral, amber, gold and jade, pearls and gems, langgan jade, turmeric, and storax.
translations.idiomatic: Many precious goods from Daqin passed through: coral, amber, gold and jade, pearls and gems, langgan jade, turmeric, and storax.

sentences.zh: 蘇合是合諸香汁煎之，非自然一物也。

translations.literal: Storax is made by boiling together the juices of various aromatics; it is not a single natural substance.
translations.idiomatic: Storax was compounded by boiling together the juices of various aromatics; it was not a single natural product.

sentences.zh: 又云大秦人采蘇合，先笮其汁以為香膏，乃賣其滓與諸國賈人，是以輾轉來達中國不大香也。

translations.literal: It is also said that when Daqin people gather storax, they first press out its juice to make fragrant ointment, then sell the dregs to merchants of various countries. For this reason, by the time it reaches China through repeated resale it is not very fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: It was also said that when people of Daqin gathered storax, they first pressed out the juice to make fragrant ointment and then sold the dregs to merchants of other lands. By the time the residue reached China through repeated resale, it was no longer very fragrant.

sentences.zh: 郁金獨出罽賓國，華色正黃而細，與芙蓉華里被蓮者相似。

translations.literal: Turmeric comes only from the country of Kapisi. Its blossoms are pure yellow and fine, resembling the lotus that grows within hibiscus blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: Turmeric came only from Kapisi. Its blossoms were a pure, fine yellow, resembling the lotus that grows within hibiscus flowers.

sentences.zh: 國人先取以上佛寺，積日槁乃糞去之，賈人以轉賣與他國也。

translations.literal: The people of the country first take it to offer at Buddhist temples. After many days it withers, and then they discard it as manure; merchants resell it to other countries.
translations.idiomatic: The people first offered it at Buddhist temples. After many days it withered and was cast away as refuse, and merchants then resold it to other countries.

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝延熹九年，大秦王安敦遣使自日南徼外來獻，漢世唯一通焉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yanxi of Emperor Huan of Han, King Andun of Daqin sent envoys from beyond the Rinan frontier to present tribute. This was the only contact of the Han dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yanxi under Emperor Huan of Han, King Andun of Daqin sent envoys from beyond the Rinan frontier to present tribute—the only such contact recorded for the Han dynasty.

sentences.zh: 其國人行賈往往至扶南、日南、交址。

translations.literal: Merchants of that country often travel as far as Funan, Rinan, and Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants from Daqin often traveled as far as Funan, Rinan, and Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 其南徼諸國人少有到大秦者。

translations.literal: People of the southern frontier states rarely reach Daqin.
translations.idiomatic: Few people from the southern frontier states ever reached Daqin.

sentences.zh: 孫權黃武五年，有大秦賈人字秦論來到交址，太守吳邈遣送詣權。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangwu of Sun Quan, a Daqin merchant named Qin Lun came to Jiaozhi. The prefect Wu Miao sent him on to Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Huangwu under Sun Quan, a Daqin merchant named Qin Lun arrived in Jiaozhi, and Prefect Wu Miao had him escorted to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 權問論方土風俗，論具以事對。

translations.literal: Quan questioned Lun about the region's geography and customs, and Lun answered in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan questioned Qin Lun about the geography and customs of his homeland, and Qin Lun answered in full.

sentences.zh: 時諸葛恪討丹陽，獲黝、歙短人。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuge Ke was campaigning against Danyang and captured short-statured people of You and She.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhuge Ke was campaigning against Danyang and captured short-statured people from You and She.

sentences.zh: 論見之曰：「大秦希見此人。」

translations.literal: When Lun saw them he said: "In Daqin such people are rarely seen."
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Lun saw them he said, "In Daqin people like this are rarely seen."

sentences.zh: 權以男女各十人，差吏會稽劉咸送論，咸於道物故，乃徑還本國也。

translations.literal: Sun Quan gave him ten men and ten women and dispatched the official Liu Xian of Kuaiji to escort Lun home. Xian died on the road, and Lun then returned directly to his own country.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan gave him ten men and ten women and dispatched the official Liu Xian of Kuaiji to escort him home. Liu Xian died on the road, and Qin Lun then returned directly to his own country.

sentences.zh: 漢和帝時，天竺數遣使貢獻，後西域反叛遂絕。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor He of Han, Tianzhu repeatedly sent envoys with tribute. Later the Western Regions rebelled and contact ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor He of Han, India repeatedly sent envoys with tribute, but after the Western Regions rebelled contact was broken off.

sentences.zh: 至桓帝延熹三年、四年，頻從日南徼外來獻，魏、晉世絕不復通。

translations.literal: By the third and fourth years of Yanxi of Emperor Huan, tribute came frequently from beyond the Rinan frontier. In the Wei and Jin eras contact ceased entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In the third and fourth years of Yanxi under Emperor Huan, envoys came frequently from beyond the Rinan frontier, but in the Wei and Jin periods contact ceased altogether.

sentences.zh: 唯吳時扶南王范旃遣親人蘇勿使其國，從扶南發投拘利口，循海大灣中正西北入，曆灣邊數國，可一年余到天竺江口，逆水行七千里乃至焉。

translations.literal: Only in Wu times did King Fan Zhan of Funan dispatch his kinsman Su Wu as envoy to that country. Setting out from Funan he put in at the mouth of Koli, followed the great bay northwestward, passed several countries along the bay's edge, and after about a year and more reached the mouth of the Tianzhu River. Sailing upstream seven thousand li, he arrived there.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Wu times did King Fan Zhan of Funan send his kinsman Su Wu as envoy to India. Setting out from Funan, he put in at the mouth of Koli and sailed northwest across the great bay, passing several countries along its shores. After more than a year he reached the mouth of the Ganges, and after another seven thousand li upstream he arrived at the capital.

sentences.zh: 天竺王驚曰：「海濱極遠，猶有此人乎！」

translations.literal: The king of Tianzhu was astonished and said: "At the farthest edge of the sea, can such people still exist!"
translations.idiomatic: The king of India was astonished and said, "At the farthest edge of the sea, can such people still exist!"

sentences.zh: 即令觀視國內，仍差陳、宋等二人以月支馬四疋報旃，勿積四年方至。

translations.literal: He immediately had them shown about the country, then dispatched Chen, Song, and two others with four Yuezhi horses to report back to Zhan. Wu took four years in all to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately had them shown about the realm, then dispatched Chen, Song, and two others with four Yuezhi horses to report back to Fan Zhan. Su Wu took four years in all to make the return journey.

sentences.zh: 其時吳遣中郎康泰使扶南，及見陳、宋等，具問天竺土俗，云：「佛道所興國也。

translations.literal: At that time Wu sent Palace Gentleman Kang Tai as envoy to Funan. When he met Chen, Song, and the others, he questioned them fully about Tianzhu's land and customs. They said: "It is the country where the Buddha Way arose.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu dispatched Palace Gentleman Kang Tai as envoy to Funan. When he met Chen, Song, and the others, he questioned them at length about the land and customs of India. They said, "It is the country where Buddhism arose.

sentences.zh: 人敦龐，土饒沃，其王號茂論。

translations.literal: The people are stout and robust; the soil is rich and fertile. Their king is titled Maolun.
translations.idiomatic: The people are stout and robust, and the soil rich and fertile. Their king bears the title Maolun.

sentences.zh: 所都城郭，水泉分流，繞于渠塹，下注大江。

translations.literal: The capital city has streams branching off and winding through canals and moats, then descending into the great river.
translations.idiomatic: The capital city had branching springs that wound through canals and moats before flowing down into the great river.

sentences.zh: 其宮殿皆雕文鐫刻。

translations.literal: Its palaces are all carved and engraved with ornamental designs.
translations.idiomatic: Its palaces were all carved and engraved with ornamental designs.

sentences.zh: 街曲市里，屋舍樓觀，鐘鼓音樂，服飾香華，水陸通流，百賈交會，器玩珍瑋，恣心所欲。

translations.literal: In winding streets and market wards stand houses, towers, and pavilions; bells, drums, and music; garments, incense, and flowers. Water and land routes connect; merchants of every kind meet in trade; vessels and curios, precious and rare—one may indulge the heart's desires.
translations.idiomatic: Winding streets and market wards were lined with houses, towers, and pavilions; bells, drums, and music filled the air; garments, incense, and flowers abounded. Water and land routes connected, merchants of every kind gathered to trade, and vessels and curios, precious and rare, were there for the taking.

sentences.zh: 左右嘉維、舍衛、葉波等十六大國。

translations.literal: To its left and right are sixteen great states such as Kashi, Shravasti, and Gandhara.
translations.idiomatic: To its left and right lay sixteen great states, including Kashi, Shravasti, and Gandhara.

sentences.zh: 去天竺或二三千里，共尊奉之，以為在天地之中。」

translations.literal: Two or three thousand li from India, they all honored and served it, believing it to lie at the center of heaven and earth."
translations.idiomatic: Two or three thousand li from India, they all honored and served it, believing it to lie at the center of heaven and earth."

sentences.zh: 天監初，其王屈多遣長史竺羅達奉表獻琉璃唾壺、雜香、古貝等物。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, its king Quduo sent Chief Clerk Zhu Luoda with a memorial presenting a glass spittoon, assorted incense, kapok cloth, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian, King Quduo sent Chief Clerk Zhu Luoda with a memorial presenting a glass spittoon, assorted incense, kapok cloth, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 天竺迦毗黎國，元嘉五年，國王月愛遣使奉表，獻金剛指環、摩勒金環諸寶物，赤白鸚鵡各一頭。

translations.literal: Kapili of Tianzhu: in the fifth year of Yuanjia, King Yue'ai sent envoys with a memorial presenting diamond finger-rings, moluo gold rings, and various precious objects, as well as one red and one white parrot.
translations.idiomatic: Kapili of India: in the fifth year of Yuanjia, King Yue'ai sent envoys with a memorial presenting diamond finger-rings, moluo gold rings, and various precious objects, along with one red and one white parrot.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始二年，又遣使貢獻，以其使主竺扶大、竺阿珍並為建威將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi of Emperor Ming, envoys were sent again with tribute. Their mission chiefs Zhu Fuda and Zhu Azhen were both appointed General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming, envoys were sent again with tribute, and their mission chiefs Zhu Fuda and Zhu Azhen were both appointed General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十八年，蘇摩黎國王那羅跋摩遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia, King Narapamoda of Sumoli sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia, King Narapamoda of Sumoli sent envoys presenting local products.

sentences.zh: 孝武孝建二年，斤陀利國王釋婆羅那鄰陀遣長史竺留陀及多獻金銀寶器。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiaowu, King Shibharanata of Gandhara sent Chief Clerk Zhu Liutuo and others to present gold, silver, and precious vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, King Shibharanata of Gandhara sent Chief Clerk Zhu Liutuo and others to present gold, silver, and precious vessels.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽元年，婆黎國遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui of the deposed emperor, Poli sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhui under the deposed emperor, Poli sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸國皆事佛道。

translations.literal: All these countries alike serve the Buddha Way.
translations.idiomatic: All these countries alike followed Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 佛道自後漢明帝法始東流，自此以來，其教稍廣，別為一家之學。

translations.literal: Since the Buddha Way first flowed east in the time of Emperor Ming of Later Han, from then on its teaching gradually spread and became a separate school of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Since Buddhism first flowed east in the time of Emperor Ming of Later Han, its teaching had gradually spread and become a distinct school of its own.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，丹陽尹蕭摹之奏曰：「佛化被於中國，已曆四代，而自頃以來，更以奢競為重。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia, Prefect of Danyang Xiao Muzhi memorialized: "The Buddha's teaching has spread over China for four dynasties already, but in recent times extravagant rivalry has become paramount.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia, Prefect of Danyang Xiao Muzhi memorialized, "The Buddha's teaching had spread over China for four dynasties already, but in recent times extravagant rivalry had become paramount.

sentences.zh: 請自今以後有欲鑄銅像者，悉詣台自聞；

translations.literal: I request that from now on anyone wishing to cast bronze images must report in person to the central administration;
translations.idiomatic: I request that from now on anyone wishing to cast bronze images must report in person to the central administration;

sentences.zh: 興造塔寺精舍，皆先列言，須許報然後就功。」

translations.literal: and that in erecting pagodas, temples, and monasteries, one must first submit a statement and may begin work only after permission is granted."
translations.idiomatic: and that in erecting pagodas, temples, and monasteries, one must first submit a statement and may begin work only after permission is granted."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又沙汰沙門罷道者數百人。

translations.literal: Monks were also screened, and several hundred who had abandoned the Way were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Monks were also screened, and several hundred who had abandoned the monastic life were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 孝武大明二年，有曇標道人與羌人高闍謀反，上因是下詔，所在精加沙汰，後有違犯，嚴其誅坐。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu, the monk Tanbiao plotted rebellion with the Qiang man Gao Ge. Because of this the emperor issued an edict ordering strict screening everywhere; thereafter violations would be punished severely.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, the monk Tanbiao plotted rebellion with the Qiang man Gao Ge. Because of this the emperor issued an edict ordering strict screening everywhere, with severe punishment for any future violations.

sentences.zh: 於是設諸條禁，自非戒行精苦，並使還俗，而諸寺尼出入宮掖，交關妃後，此制竟不能行。

translations.literal: Various prohibitions were then established: except for those of strict and arduous discipline, all were made to return to lay life. Yet nuns of the various temples entered and left the palace quarters and maintained relations with consorts and empresses—this regulation could not be enforced after all.
translations.idiomatic: Various prohibitions were then established: except for those of strict and arduous discipline, all were made to return to lay life. Yet nuns of the various temples entered and left the palace quarters and maintained relations with consorts and empresses—this regulation could not be enforced after all.

sentences.zh: 先是，晉世庾冰始創議欲使沙門敬王者，後桓玄復述其義，並不果行。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Jin times Yu Bing first proposed that monks should show respect to the ruler; later Huan Xuan restated the argument. Neither proposal was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Jin times Yu Bing had first proposed that monks should show respect to the ruler; later Huan Xuan had restated the argument. Neither proposal was carried out.

sentences.zh: 大明六年，孝武使有司奏沙門接見皆盡敬，詔可。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daming, Emperor Xiaowu had the relevant offices memorialize that monks should show full respect when received in audience. The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daming, Emperor Xiaowu had the relevant offices memorialize that monks should show full respect when received in audience, and the edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初復舊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the deposed emperor's reign the former practice was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the deposed emperor's reign the former practice was restored.

sentences.zh: 孝武寵姬殷貴妃薨，為之立寺，貴妃子子鸞封新安王，故以新安為寺號。

translations.literal: The favored consort Consort Yin of Emperor Xiaowu died, and a temple was erected for her. Her son by the consort, Ziluan, was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an, so Xin'an was taken as the temple's name.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu's favored consort, Consort Yin, died, a temple was erected for her. Her son Ziluan was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an, and Xin'an was taken as the temple's name.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝殺子鸞，乃毀廢新安寺，驅斥僧徒，尋又毀中興、天寶諸寺。

translations.literal: The deposed emperor killed Ziluan, then destroyed and abolished Xin'an Temple and drove out the monks. Soon afterward he also destroyed the Zhongxing, Tianbao, and other temples.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor killed Ziluan, then destroyed Xin'an Temple and drove out the monks. Soon afterward he also destroyed the Zhongxing, Tianbao, and other temples.

sentences.zh: 明帝定亂，下令修復。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming suppressed the rebellion, he ordered restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming suppressed the rebellion, he ordered the temples restored.

sentences.zh: 宋世名僧有道生道人，彭城人，父為廣戚令。

translations.literal: Among the famous monks of the Song was the monk Daosheng, a native of Pengcheng. His father served as magistrate of Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: Among the famous monks of the Song was Daosheng, a native of Pengcheng whose father had served as magistrate of Guangqi.

sentences.zh: 道生為沙門法大弟子，幼而聰悟。

translations.literal: Daosheng was the chief disciple of the monk Fada and was clever and perceptive from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng was the chief disciple of the monk Fada and had been clever and perceptive from childhood.

sentences.zh: 年十五便能講經，及長有異解，立頓悟義，時人推服。

translations.literal: At fifteen he could already expound the sutras. When grown he had unusual interpretations and established the doctrine of sudden enlightenment, which people of the time admired.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he could already expound the sutras. When grown he developed unusual interpretations and established the doctrine of sudden enlightenment, which people of the time admired.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十一年，卒於廬山，沙門慧琳為之誄。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia he died on Mount Lu. The monk Huilin composed a eulogy for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia he died on Mount Lu, and the monk Huilin composed a eulogy for him.

sentences.zh: 慧琳者，秦郡秦縣人，姓劉氏。

translations.literal: Huilin was a native of Qin County in Qin Commandery, surname Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Huilin was a native of Qin County in Qin Commandery, of the Liu clan.

sentences.zh: 少出家，住冶城寺。

translations.literal: He left home young and resided at Ye City Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He left home at a young age and resided at Ye City Temple.

sentences.zh: 有才章，兼內外之學，為廬陵王義真所知。

translations.literal: He had literary talent and combined inner and outer learning. Prince Yizhen of Luling came to know him.
translations.idiomatic: He had literary talent and combined Buddhist and secular learning, and came to be known by Prince Yizhen of Luling.

sentences.zh: 嘗著均善論，頗貶裁佛法，云：「有白學先生，以為中國聖人經綸百世，其德弘矣，智周萬變，天人之理盡矣。

translations.literal: He once wrote the Treatise on Equal Goodness, which rather criticized and judged the Buddha Dharma, saying: "There is a master of White Learning who holds that the sages of China have governed for a hundred generations; their virtue is vast, their wisdom encompasses myriad changes, and the principles of Heaven and man are fully exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote the Treatise on Equal Goodness, which rather criticized Buddhism, saying, "There is a master of White Learning who holds that the sages of China have governed for a hundred generations; their virtue is vast, their wisdom encompasses myriad changes, and the principles of Heaven and man are fully exhausted.

sentences.zh: 道無隱旨，教罔遺筌，聰叡迪哲，何負於殊論哉。

translations.literal: The Way has no hidden meaning; teaching leaves no fish-trap behind. The wise and enlightened—what do they owe to foreign doctrines?
translations.idiomatic: The Way has no hidden meaning; teaching leaves no essential untold. What need have the wise and enlightened for foreign doctrines?

sentences.zh: 有黑學道士陋之，謂不照幽冥之塗，弗及來生之化，雖尚虛心，未能虛事，不逮西域之深也。」

translations.literal: A master of Black Learning despises this, saying it does not illuminate the path of the dark underworld and falls short of transformation in lives to come. Though it honors empty mind, it cannot empty affairs—it does not reach the depth of the Western Regions."
translations.idiomatic: A master of Black Learning despises this, saying it does not illuminate the path of the dark underworld and falls short of transformation in lives to come. Though it honors empty mind, it cannot empty affairs—it does not reach the depth of the Western Regions."

sentences.zh: 為客主酬答，其歸以為「六度與五教並行，信順與慈悲齊立」。

translations.literal: He set forth guest and host in mutual response, and concluded that "the six perfections and the five teachings proceed together; faith and obedience stand alongside compassion and mercy."
translations.idiomatic: He set forth guest and host in mutual response and concluded that "the six perfections and the five teachings proceed together; faith and obedience stand alongside compassion and mercy."

sentences.zh: 論行於世。

translations.literal: The treatise circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The treatise circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 舊僧謂其敗黜釋氏，欲加擯斥。

translations.literal: Older monks said it degraded and dismissed the Shakya clan and wished to have him ostracized.
translations.idiomatic: Older monks said it degraded Buddhism and wished to have him ostracized.

sentences.zh: 文帝見論賞之，元嘉中，遂參權要，朝廷大事皆與議焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen read the treatise and praised it. In the Yuanjia era he came to participate in power, and major affairs of court were all discussed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen read the treatise and praised it. In the Yuanjia era Huilin came to participate in power, and major affairs of court were all discussed with him.

sentences.zh: 賓客輻湊，門車常有數十兩。

translations.literal: Guests gathered like wheel spokes; there were often several dozen carriages at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Guests gathered in crowds, and there were often several dozen carriages at his gate.

sentences.zh: 四方贈賂相系，勢傾一時。

translations.literal: Gifts and bribes from all directions followed one after another; his influence eclipsed his age.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts and bribes from all directions followed one after another, and his influence eclipsed his age.

sentences.zh: 方筵七八，座上恒滿。

translations.literal: Banquet tables numbered seven or eight; his seats were always full.
translations.idiomatic: He kept seven or eight banquet tables, and his seats were always full.

sentences.zh: 琳著高屐，披貂裘，置通呈書佐，權侔宰輔。

translations.literal: Huilin wore high clogs and draped himself in a sable fur. He kept clerks to receive petitions and present documents; his power matched that of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Huilin wore high clogs and draped himself in sable fur, kept clerks to receive petitions and present documents, and wielded power equal to a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 會稽孔覬嘗詣之，遇賓客填咽，暄敘而已。

translations.literal: Kong Yi of Kuaiji once called on him and found guests packed to suffocation; there was only noisy conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yi of Kuaiji once called on him and found guests packed in so tightly that there was only noisy conversation.

sentences.zh: 覬慨然曰：「遂有黑衣宰相，可謂冠屨失所矣。」

translations.literal: Yi said with indignation: "Now there is a black-robed chief minister—one might say caps and shoes have lost their proper places."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yi said with indignation, "Now there is a black-robed chief minister—one might say caps and shoes have lost their proper places."

sentences.zh: 注孝經及莊子逍遙篇文論傳於世。

translations.literal: He annotated the Classic of Filial Piety and wrote a literary treatise on the "Free and Easy Wandering" chapter of Zhuangzi, both of which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also annotated the Classic of Filial Piety and wrote a literary treatise on the "Free and Easy Wandering" chapter of Zhuangzi, both of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 又有慧嚴、慧議道人，並住東安寺。

translations.literal: There were also the monks Huiyan and Huiyi, both residing at Dong'an Temple.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the monks Huiyan and Huiyi, both residing at Dong'an Temple.

sentences.zh: 學行精整，為道俗所推。

translations.literal: Their learning and conduct were refined and orderly; monks and laypeople alike esteemed them.
translations.idiomatic: Their learning and conduct were refined and orderly, and monks and laypeople alike esteemed them.

sentences.zh: 時鬥場寺多禪僧，都下為之語曰：「鬥場禪師窟，東安談義林。」

translations.literal: At that time Dou Chang Temple had many Chan monks, and people in the capital said of them: "Dou Chang is the cave of Chan masters; Dong'an is the grove of doctrinal discourse."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dou Chang Temple had many Chan monks, and people in the capital said, "Dou Chang is the cave of Chan masters; Dong'an is the grove of doctrinal discourse."

sentences.zh: 孝武大明四年，于中興寺設齋，有一異僧，眾莫之識，問名，答言名明慧，從天安寺來。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu, a vegetarian feast was held at Zhongxing Temple. There was a strange monk whom no one recognized. Asked his name, he answered that he was called Minghui and had come from Tian'an Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, a vegetarian feast was held at Zhongxing Temple. There was a strange monk whom no one recognized. Asked his name, he answered that he was called Minghui and had come from Tian'an Temple.

sentences.zh: 忽然不見。

translations.literal: Suddenly he vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he vanished.

sentences.zh: 天下無此寺名，乃改中興曰天安寺。

translations.literal: There was no temple by that name anywhere in the realm, so Zhongxing was renamed Tian'an Temple.
translations.idiomatic: There was no temple by that name anywhere in the realm, so Zhongxing was renamed Tian'an Temple.

sentences.zh: 大明中，外國沙門摩訶衍苦節有精理，於都下出新經勝鬘經，尤見重釋學。

translations.literal: In the Daming era, the foreign monk Mahayana, austere in discipline and refined in doctrine, brought out in the capital the new sutra Shorter Sutra of Queen Shrimala, which was especially valued in Buddhist studies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era, the foreign monk Mahayana, austere in discipline and refined in doctrine, brought out in the capital the new sutra Shorter Sutra of Queen Shrimala, which was especially valued in Buddhist studies.

sentences.zh: 師子國

translations.literal: Lion Country
translations.idiomatic: Lion Country

sentences.zh: 師子國，天竺旁國也。

translations.literal: Lion Country is a neighboring state of Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Lion Country was a neighboring state of India.

sentences.zh: 其地和適，無冬夏之異。

translations.literal: Its land is mild and temperate; there is no difference between winter and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Its land was mild and temperate, with no difference between winter and summer.

sentences.zh: 五穀隨人種，不須時節。

translations.literal: The five grains may be planted whenever people sow them; seasons need not be observed.
translations.idiomatic: The five grains could be planted whenever people sowed them, without regard to season.

sentences.zh: 其國舊無人，止有鬼神及龍居之。

translations.literal: Formerly the country had no human inhabitants; only spirits and dragons dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the country had no human inhabitants; only spirits and dragons dwelt there.

sentences.zh: 諸國商估來共市易，鬼神不見其形，但出珍寶，顯其所堪價。

translations.literal: Merchants of various countries came to trade together. The spirits did not show their forms but produced precious things and displayed the prices they would accept.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants of various countries came to trade. The spirits did not show themselves but produced precious goods and displayed the prices they would accept.

sentences.zh: 商人依價取之。

translations.literal: Merchants took them according to the price.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants took the goods according to the stated price.

sentences.zh: 諸國人聞其土樂，因此競至，或有住者，遂成大國。

translations.literal: When people of various countries heard that its land was pleasant, they raced to come. Some settled there, and it gradually became a great state.
translations.idiomatic: When people of various countries heard that its land was pleasant, they raced to come. Some settled there, and it gradually became a great state.

sentences.zh: 晉義熙初，始遣使獻玉像，經十載乃至。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi of Jin, envoys were first sent presenting a jade image. After ten years it arrived.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yixi under Jin, envoys were first sent presenting a jade image. After ten years it arrived.

sentences.zh: 像高四尺二寸，玉色潔潤，形制殊特，殆非人工。

translations.literal: The image was four feet two inches high. The jade's color was pure and lustrous; its form was extraordinary—hardly the work of human hands.
translations.idiomatic: The image stood four feet two inches high. The jade was pure and lustrous, its form extraordinary—hardly the work of human hands.

sentences.zh: 此像曆晉、宋在瓦官寺，先有征士戴安道手制佛像五軀，及顧長康維摩畫圖，世人號之三絕。

translations.literal: This image remained at Waguan Temple through Jin and Song. There were already five Buddha images made by the recluse Dai Andao and Gu Kaizhi's painting of Vimalakirti; people of the time called them the three supreme works.
translations.idiomatic: This image remained at Waguan Temple through Jin and Song. There were already five Buddha images made by the recluse Dai Andao and Gu Kaizhi's painting of Vimalakirti; people of the time called them the three supreme works.

sentences.zh: 至齊東昏遂毀玉像，前截臂，次取身，為嬖妾潘貴妃作釵釧。

translations.literal: By the time of Donghun of Qi, the jade image was destroyed: first the arms were cut off, then the body was taken, and hairpins and bracelets were made for the favorite consort Consort Pan.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Donghun of Qi, the jade image was destroyed: first the arms were cut off, then the body was taken, and hairpins and bracelets were made for the favorite consort, Consort Pan.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉五年，其王刹利摩訶遣使奉表貢獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanjia under Song, King Shakramati sent envoys presenting a memorial and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanjia under Song, King Shakramati sent envoys with a memorial and tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二年，又遣使奉獻。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, envoys were again sent with offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, tribute envoys were sent again.

sentences.zh: 梁大通元年，後王迦葉伽羅訶黎邪使使奉表貢獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong under Liang, the later king Kasyapa Galoheliya sent envoys presenting a memorial and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong under Liang, the later king Kasyapa Galoheliya sent envoys with a memorial and tribute.
